words.ex: The king decided to abdicate in favor of his son.
words.ex_cn: 国王决定退位，让位给他的儿子。
words.en: If a king or queen abdicates, he or she gives up being king or queen.

words.ex: The boy has an abnormal heartbeat.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩的心跳不正常。
words.en: Deviating from what is normal or usual, typically in a way that is undesirable or worrying.

words.ex: The government decided to abolish the old law.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定废除这项旧法律。
words.en: If someone in authority abolishes a system or practice, they formally put an end to it.

words.ex: His absenteeism caused the team to lose points.
words.ex_cn: 他的缺勤导致团队丢了分数。
words.en: Absenteeism is the habitual non-presence of an employee at their job.

words.ex: The sponge absorbs water quickly.
words.ex_cn: 海绵很快吸收水。
words.en: If something absorbs a liquid, gas, or other substance, it soaks it up or takes it in.

words.tr:
adj. 抽象的；非具体的；
n. 摘要；概要；抽象派艺术作品；
words.ex: The painting shows an abstract shape.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画展示了一个抽象的形状。
words.en: An abstract idea or way of thinking is based on general ideas rather than on real things and events.

words.tr: adj. 荒唐的；荒唐可笑的；
words.ex: It's absurd to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套是荒唐的。
words.en: If you say that something is absurd, you are criticizing it because you think that it is ridiculous or that it does not make sense.

words.ex: The forest has abundant water and trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林水源和树木都很丰富。
words.en: If something is abundant, there is a lot of it or it is very common.

words.tr:
adj. 学术的；
n. 大学教师；学者；
words.ex: He published an academic paper on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇关于气候变化的学术论文。
words.en: relating to education, especially at college or university level

words.ex: The car will accelerate when you press the gas.
words.ex_cn: 当你踩油门时，汽车会加速。
words.en: To accelerate means to start to go faster or to make something start to go faster.

words.tr:
n. 接触（的机会或权利）；进入；通道；
v. 获取；使用；接近；
words.ex: Students need access to the library.
words.ex_cn: 学生需要有接触图书馆的机会。
words.en: If you have access to a building or other place, you are able to enter it or use it.

words.tr: adj. 易接近的；可使用的；简单易懂的；可进入的；
words.ex: The park is accessible by bus.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园乘公交车可达。
words.en: If a place or building is accessible to people, it is easy for them to reach it or get into it. If an object is accessible, it is easy to reach.

words.ex: The actor received acclaim for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而受到赞扬。
words.en: If someone or something is acclaimed, they are praised enthusiastically and publicly.

words.tr: v. 容纳；适应；为...提供住宿；
words.ex: The hotel can accommodate 200 guests.
words.ex_cn: 这家酒店能容纳200位客人。
words.en: If a building or space can accommodate someone or something, it has enough room for them.

words.ex: The singer sang with piano accompaniment.
words.ex_cn: 歌手在钢琴伴奏下演唱。
words.en: An accompaniment is a musical part which supports or partners a solo instrument, voice, or group.

words.ex: He worked hard to accomplish his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以实现自己的目标。
words.en: To accomplish something means to succeed in doing it, especially after a lot of effort.

words.ex: The two countries signed an accord to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项协议以停止战争。
words.en: An accord is an official agreement or treaty. It can also refer to a state of agreement or harmony.

words.ex: He was late, so he left accordingly.
words.ex_cn: 他迟到了，于是相应地提前出发了。
words.en: In a way that is appropriate to the particular circumstances.

words.ex: He works as an accountant in a small company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家小公司当会计师。
words.en: An accountant is a person whose job is to keep, inspect, and analyze financial accounts.

words.tr: v. 解释说明；“account”的现在分词； n. 会计；会计学；
words.ex: He is accounting for his absence.
words.ex_cn: 他正在解释他的缺席。
words.en: Accounting is the process of keeping financial accounts.

words.tr: n. 自然增加；增加之物；增值
words.ex: The accretion of sand formed a small beach.
words.ex_cn: 沙子的堆积形成了一个小海滩。
words.en: Accretion is the process of growth or increase, typically by the gradual accumulation of additional layers or matter.

words.ex: Interest will accrue over time.
words.ex_cn: 利息会随着时间积累。
words.en: If money or interest accrues, it gradually increases in amount over a period of time.

words.ex: He accumulates coins from different countries.
words.ex_cn: 他收集来自不同国家的硬币。
words.en: To accumulate means to gradually gather or acquire an increasing number or quantity of something.

words.ex: The accuracy of the clock is very high.
words.ex_cn: 这个钟的精确性很高。
words.en: The quality or state of being correct or precise.

words.ex: The clock shows accurate time.
words.ex_cn: 这个钟显示的时间很精确。
words.en: Correct in all details; exact.

words.tr: adj. 习惯的；惯常的； v. “accustom”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is accustomed to waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 他习惯早起。
words.en: If you are accustomed to something, you know it so well or have experienced it so often that it seems natural, unsurprising, or easy to deal with.

words.ex: The acidity of lemon juice is very high.
words.ex_cn: 柠檬汁的酸性很强。
words.en: Acidity is the level of acid in substances such as water, soil, or wine.

words.ex: He finally acknowledged his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you acknowledge a fact or a situation, you accept or admit that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: The room has good acoustic properties.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间有良好的声音效果。
words.en: Relating to sound or the sense of hearing.

words.ex: The room has acoustical panels to improve sound.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间有声学面板来改善声音。
words.en: Relating to the science of sound, including its production, transmission, and effects.

words.ex: He acquiesced to his boss's decision.
words.ex_cn: 他默许了老板的决定。
words.en: If you acquiesce in something, you agree to do what someone wants or to accept what they do even though you may not agree with it.

words.ex: He acquired a new skill last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年获得了一项新技能。
words.en: If you acquire something, you buy or obtain it for yourself, or someone gives it to you.

words.tr: n. 获得；得到的东西；收购；
words.ex: The acquisition of new skills takes time.
words.ex_cn: 获得新技能需要时间。
words.en: An acquisition is something that someone buys, often to add to a collection of things.

words.ex: The farm has an acreage of 50 acres.
words.ex_cn: 这个农场的土地面积是50英亩。
words.en: Acreage is the area of land measured in acres.

words.tr: v. 激活；使活动；使活化；
words.ex: Press the button to activate the device.
words.ex_cn: 按下按钮来激活设备。
words.en: If a device or process is activated, it starts working or becomes operational.

words.ex: His activism helped change the law.
words.ex_cn: 他的行动主义帮助改变了法律。
words.en: Activism is the policy or action of using vigorous campaigning to bring about political or social change.

words.ex: He is an activist who helps the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位帮助穷人的积极分子。
words.en: An activist is a person who works to bring about political or social change by campaigning, public speaking, or demonstrating.

words.tr: adj. 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；
words.ex: He has an acute mind and solves problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他思维敏锐，能快速解决问题。
words.en: An acute problem or negative feeling is very severe.

words.ex: He adapted to the new school quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快就适应了新学校。
words.en: To make suitable to or fit for a specific use or situation.

words.ex: The adaptation of animals to cold weather is amazing.
words.ex_cn: 动物对寒冷天气的适应令人惊叹。
words.en: An adaptation is a film, television drama, or stage play that is based on a written work.

words.tr: n. 改编者；适配器；多头电源插座
words.ex: He is an adapter of classic novels into movies.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位将经典小说改编成电影的改编者。
words.en: An adapter is a device that enables different pieces of electrical equipment to be used together, or that allows a device to connect to a power source.

words.ex: He is an addict who cannot stop smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他是个无法戒烟的瘾君子。
words.en: An addict is someone who is unable to stop taking harmful drugs, or someone who is very interested in something and spends a lot of time doing it.

words.ex: The game is addictive and hard to stop playing.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏令人上瘾，很难停止玩。
words.en: If a substance or activity is addictive, it makes you want more of it so that you become dependent on it.

words.ex: The addition of a new chair made the room more comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 增加一把新椅子让房间更舒适了。
words.en: An addition is something that is added to something else, often to improve it or make it larger.

words.ex: This food contains a harmless additive for flavor.
words.ex_cn: 这种食物含有用于调味的无害添加物。
words.en: An additive is a substance which is added in small amounts to something else in order to improve it, preserve it, or make it more effective.

words.ex: He is adept at solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长解决数学问题。
words.en: Someone who is adept at something is very skilled at it.

words.ex: He adheres to his principles even when it's hard.
words.ex_cn: 即使很难，他仍然坚持自己的原则。
words.en: If you adhere to a rule or agreement, you act in the way that it says you should.

words.ex: The adherence of the sticker to the wall is strong.
words.ex_cn: 贴纸对墙的粘附很强。
words.en: Adherence is the act of following or sticking to a particular set of beliefs, principles, or rules.

words.ex: The two houses are adjacent to each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两栋房子彼此相邻。
words.en: If one thing is adjacent to another, it is next to it or adjoining it.

words.tr: v. 调整；使适合；使适应；
words.ex: He adjusted the chair to sit comfortably.
words.ex_cn: 他调整了椅子以便坐得舒服。
words.en: To adjust something means to change it so that it is more effective or appropriate, or so that it fits better.

words.tr: v. 给予（药物或治疗）；管理；实施；
words.ex: The nurse will administer the medicine to the patient.
words.ex_cn: 护士会给病人服药。
words.en: To administer means to manage or oversee the execution, use, or conduct of something; to dispense or apply (a remedy or drug).

words.ex: He finally admit his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you admit that something bad, unpleasant, or embarrassing is true, you agree, often unwillingly, that it is true.

words.tr:
n. 青少年；
adj. 青少年的；
words.ex: The adolescent walked to school with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 这个青少年和朋友们一起走路去上学。
words.en: An adolescent is a young person who is developing into an adult.

words.ex: The company made the adoption of new technology quickly.
words.ex_cn: 公司迅速采用了新技术。
words.en: The act of legally taking another's child and bringing it up as one's own, or the act of accepting something new.

words.ex: The advent of smartphones changed how we communicate.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的到来改变了我们的交流方式。
words.en: The arrival of a notable person, thing, or event.

words.ex: The adverse weather delayed the flight.
words.ex_cn: 不利的天气延误了航班。
words.en: If something is adverse, it is harmful or unfavorable.

words.tr: n. 广告活动；广告业； v. 做广告；“advertise”的现在分词；
words.ex: The company launched a new advertising campaign last month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司上个月推出了一项新的广告活动。
words.en: The activity of producing advertisements for commercial products or services.

words.ex: He supports advocacy for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他支持清洁用水的倡导。
words.en: The act of pleading or arguing in favor of something, such as a cause, idea, or policy; active support.

words.ex: The disease afflicted many people in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病使村子里许多人遭受痛苦。
words.en: If you are afflicted by pain, illness, or misfortune, it causes you great suffering and distress.

words.ex: The affluent family bought a big house by the lake.
words.ex_cn: 这个富裕的家庭在湖边买了一栋大房子。
words.en: Having a great deal of money; wealthy.

words.ex: This phone is affordable for students.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机对学生来说价格合理。
words.en: If something is affordable, most people have enough money to buy it.

words.ex: The aftermath of the storm left many trees down.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，许多树被吹倒了。
words.en: The aftermath of an important event, especially a harmful one, is the situation that results from it.

words.ex: Loud noise aggravates his headache.
words.ex_cn: 噪音加重了他的头痛。
words.en: If someone or something aggravates a situation, they make it worse.

words.tr:
n. 总计；集合体
adj. 合计的；总的
v. （使）聚集；聚合；总计为
words.ex: The aggregate of all sales this month is $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 本月所有销售额的总计是5万美元。
words.en: An aggregate is a number of things or people that are considered as a group or a whole.

words.ex: The aggression of the army caused many deaths.
words.ex_cn: 军队的侵略导致了许多人死亡。
words.en: Aggression is a violent or hostile behavior towards another person or country.

words.tr: adj. 攻击性的；有进取心的；侵略性的；
words.ex: The dog showed aggressive behavior toward strangers.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗对陌生人表现出攻击性行为。
words.en: An aggressive person or animal has a quality of anger and determination that makes them ready to attack others.

words.ex: The country has an agrarian economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家有一个农业经济。
words.en: Relating to land, especially agricultural land, or to the ownership or division of such land.

words.ex: He had a minor ailment and stayed home from work.
words.ex_cn: 他得了一点小病，没去上班。
words.en: An ailment is a minor illness or health problem.

words.ex: The airliner landed safely at the airport.
words.ex_cn: 这架客机安全地降落在机场。
words.en: A large commercial airplane designed to carry passengers on scheduled flights.

words.ex: He drank a glass of ale at the pub.
words.ex_cn: 他在酒吧喝了一杯麦芽酒。
words.en: Ale is a type of beer that is brewed using a warm fermentation method, resulting in a sweet, full-bodied and fruity taste.

words.ex: The pond is full of green alga.
words.ex_cn: 池塘里充满了绿色的藻类。
words.en: A simple, nonflowering, and typically aquatic plant of a large group that includes the seaweeds and many single-celled forms. Algae contain chlorophyll but lack true stems, roots, leaves, and vascular tissue.

words.tr:
n. 外星人；外国人；外侨；
adj. 外国的；陌生的；相异的；
words.ex: The boy saw an alien in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在森林里看到了一个外星人。
words.en: An alien is someone who is not a citizen of the country in which they live, or a creature from outer space.

words.ex: The engineer checked the alignment of the wheels.
words.ex_cn: 工程师检查了车轮的对齐。
words.en: The arrangement of something in a straight line or in correct relative positions.

words.ex: She sang softly to allay his fears.
words.ex_cn: 她轻声唱歌以缓解他的恐惧。
words.en: If you allay someone's fears or doubts, you stop them feeling afraid or doubtful.

words.ex: He alleges that the manager stole money.
words.ex_cn: 他声称经理偷了钱。
words.en: If you allege that something bad is true, you say it but do not prove it.

words.ex: He swore allegiance to his country.
words.ex_cn: 他向自己的国家宣誓效忠。
words.en: Loyalty or commitment to a superior or to a group or cause.

words.ex: He is allergic to peanuts.
words.ex_cn: 他对花生过敏。
words.en: If you are allergic to something, you become ill or get a rash when you eat it, smell it, or touch it.

words.ex: He has an allergy to peanuts.
words.ex_cn: 他对花生过敏。
words.en: An allergy is a condition in which your immune system reacts abnormally to a foreign substance.

words.ex: Drugs can alleviate pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To make something less severe or intense.

words.ex: The two countries formed an alliance to fight the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家结成联盟以对抗敌人。
words.en: An alliance is a group of countries or political parties that are formally united and working together because they have similar aims.

words.ex: The alligator swims slowly in the river.
words.ex_cn: 鳄鱼在河里慢慢游动。
words.en: An alligator is a large reptile with a long body, thick skin, and a long tail, living in the water and on land in the hot wet parts of America and China.

words.ex: The teacher will allocate books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将给学生分配书籍。
words.en: To allocate something means to give it to a particular person or use it for a particular purpose.

words.ex: Each family was given an allotment of land to farm.
words.ex_cn: 每个家庭都被分配了一块土地来耕种。
words.en: An allotment is a share or portion of something that has been divided or distributed.

words.ex: My parents give me a weekly allowance.
words.ex_cn: 我父母每周给我零用钱。
words.en: An allowance is money that is given regularly, usually to a child, by their parents, or by the government to someone who is unemployed or ill.

words.tr: v. 暗指；（间接）提到；影射
words.ex: He alluded to the problem without naming it.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示了这个问题，但没有点明。
words.en: To allude to something means to mention it in an indirect way.

words.tr: n. 希腊字母表的第一个字母；甲，α项，α类（一系列项目、分类中的第一位，如化合物的第一种形式）；（...
words.ex: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet.
words.ex_cn: Alpha是希腊字母表中的第一个字母。
words.en: The first letter of the Greek alphabet, often used to denote the first or most significant in a series or group.

words.ex: He will alter the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会改动计划。
words.en: To alter something means to change it, usually slightly, or to cause the characteristics of something to change.

words.tr:
adj. 交替的；轮流的；间隔的；
v. （使）交替；（使）轮流；
words.ex: We take alternate days off work.
words.ex_cn: 我们隔天休息一次。
words.en: If something alternates between two things, it repeatedly changes from one to the other and back again.

words.tr: n. 替代选择；替代选择（alternative 的复数）；
words.ex: We need to find better alternatives to plastic.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要找到比塑料更好的替代选择。
words.en: An alternative is something that you can choose to do or use instead of something else.

words.ex: The village is at an altitude of 2,000 meters.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄的海拔是2000米。
words.en: The height of an object or point in relation to sea level or ground level.

words.ex: His altruism made him donate all his money to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他的利他主义让他把所有钱捐给了穷人。
words.en: Altruism is the belief in or practice of disinterested and selfless concern for the well-being of others.

words.ex: He uses aluminum foil to wrap the food.
words.ex_cn: 他用铝箔纸包食物。
words.en: A light, silvery metal that is used especially for making cooking equipment and aircraft parts.

words.ex: She is an alumna of Harvard University.
words.ex_cn: 她是哈佛大学的校友。
words.en: An alumna is a female former student of a particular school, college, or university.

words.ex: He is an alumnus of Harvard University.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的男毕业生。
words.en: An alumnus is a former student of a particular school, college, or university.

words.ex: The dentist used an amalgam to fill the cavity.
words.ex_cn: 牙医用汞合金填补了蛀牙。
words.en: An amalgam is a mixture of mercury and another metal, especially one used by dentists to fill holes in teeth. It can also refer to a mixture of different things.

words.ex: He amass wealth by working hard.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作积累财富。
words.en: If you amass something such as money or information, you gradually collect a large amount of it.

words.tr:
n. 业余爱好者；
adj. 业余的；
words.ex: He is an amateur who paints on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他是个周末画画的业余爱好者。
words.en: An amateur is someone who does something as a hobby and not as a job.

words.ex: She wore a necklace made of amber.
words.ex_cn: 她戴了一条琥珀制成的项链。
words.en: Amber is a hard, translucent, yellowish-brown substance that is used for making jewelry or other objects. It is formed from the resin of ancient trees.

words.ex: The sentence has ambiguity because it can mean two things.
words.ex_cn: 这句话有歧义，因为它可以有两种意思。
words.en: If you say that there is ambiguity in something, you mean that it is unclear or confusing, or it can be understood in more than one way.

words.ex: He felt ambivalent about accepting the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对接受这份工作邀约感到矛盾。
words.en: If you say that someone is ambivalent about something, you mean that they have mixed feelings about it or are unsure whether they want it or not.

words.ex: He is amenable to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意接受新想法。
words.en: If you are amenable to something, you are willing to do it or accept it.

words.ex: He amended the letter before sending it.
words.ex_cn: 他在发送信件之前修正了它。
words.en: To amend something means to make changes to it in order to improve it or make it more accurate.

words.tr: n. 便利设施；舒适条件；公共设施；
words.ex: The apartment has good amenities like a gym and a swimming pool.
words.ex_cn: 这套公寓有健身房和游泳池等便利设施。
words.en: An amenity is something that makes a place more pleasant or comfortable to live in.

words.ex: Proteins are made of amino acids.
words.ex_cn: 蛋白质由氨基酸组成。
words.en: An amino acid is a type of organic acid that contains both a carboxyl group and an amino group, and is a basic component of proteins.

words.tr: n. 圆形剧场；竞技场；梯形教室
words.ex: The students watched a play in the old amphitheater.
words.ex_cn: 学生们在旧的圆形剧场里观看了戏剧。
words.en: An amphitheater is a large open area surrounded by rows of seats sloping upwards. Amphitheaters were used in ancient Greece and Rome for public entertainments.

words.ex: This is a good example of teamwork.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个团队合作的好例子。
words.en: An example is a particular instance of something that is representative of a group or used to illustrate a point.

words.ex: The guitar amplifier makes the sound louder.
words.ex_cn: 吉他放大器让声音变大。
words.en: An amplifier is an electronic device that increases the strength of electrical signals, especially sound signals.

words.ex: The speaker will amplify the sound for everyone to hear.
words.ex_cn: 扬声器会放大声音，让每个人都能听到。
words.en: To amplify something means to make it louder, stronger, or more detailed.

words.ex: The amplitude of the sound is very high.
words.ex_cn: 声音的振幅非常高。
words.en: The extent or range of a quality, property, process, or phenomenon: magnitude.

words.ex: Anaerobic bacteria can live without oxygen.
words.ex_cn: 无氧细菌可以在没有氧气的情况下生存。
words.en: relating to or requiring an absence of free oxygen

words.tr:
n. 类似物
adj. 模拟的；指针式的
words.ex: The clock has analog hands.
words.ex_cn: 这个钟有指针。
words.en: An analog is something that is similar to something else in design, origin, use, etc., but is not exactly the same.

words.ex: This old phone is an analogue of the new smartphone.
words.ex_cn: 这部旧手机是这款智能手机的类似物。
words.en: Something that is similar to another thing in design, origin, use, etc., but not exactly the same.

words.ex: He used an analogy to explain how the heart works.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个类比来解释心脏是如何工作的。
words.en: If you make or draw an analogy between two things, you show that they are similar in some way.

words.ex: He uses analytic methods to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他使用解析方法来解决这个问题。
words.en: Analytic refers to the process of breaking down complex information or substances into smaller parts in order to understand or examine them.

words.tr: adj. 分析的；善于分析的；
words.ex: He uses analytical skills to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用分析能力解决数学问题。
words.en: An analytical way of doing something involves the use of logical reasoning.

words.ex: The doctor studied the anatomical structure of the heart.
words.ex_cn: 医生研究了心脏的解剖结构。
words.en: Relating to the structure of the bodies of people and animals.

words.ex: His argument is based on anecdotal evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点基于轶事证据。
words.en: Anecdotal evidence is based on personal accounts rather than on research that can be verified.

words.ex: He felt animosity toward his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对邻居感到敌意。
words.en: Animosity is a strong feeling of dislike and anger towards someone.

words.ex: The teacher will announce the results tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天将宣布结果。
words.en: To announce something means to make it known publicly or officially.

words.ex: The school made an announcement about the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 学校发布了关于假期的通告。
words.en: A public or formal notice about something that has happened or is going to happen.

words.tr: n. 变色龙，变色蜥，安乐蜥
words.ex: An anole lizard climbs the tree.
words.ex_cn: 一只安乐蜥爬上了树。
words.en: A small lizard, especially one of the genus Anolis, native to the Americas, known for its ability to change color.

words.tr: n. 异常事物；反常现象；
words.ex: The strange weather this month is an anomaly.
words.ex_cn: 这个月奇怪的天气是一个异常现象。
words.en: Something that deviates from what is standard, normal, or expected.

words.ex: He posted an anonymous comment online.
words.ex_cn: 他在网上发布了一条匿名评论。
words.en: If you remain anonymous when you do something, you do not let people know that you were the person who did it.

words.tr: adj. 应负责任的；可回答的；有责任的
words.ex: The manager is answerable for the company's performance.
words.ex_cn: 经理应对公司的业绩负责。
words.en: If you are answerable to someone for something that you do, you are responsible for it and must be prepared to justify your actions to them.

words.tr: n. 对抗；对立；敌对状态（行为）
words.ex: There is antagonism between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这两个邻居之间有敌意。
words.en: Antagonism is a strong feeling of dislike or opposition towards someone or something.

words.ex: He antedated the contract by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他把合同的日期提前了一周。
words.en: To be of an earlier date than something else; to precede in time.

words.tr: adj. 前面的；前部的；较早的
words.ex: The anterior part of the brain controls movement.
words.ex_cn: 大脑的前部控制运动。
words.en: Located before or at the front of something.

words.ex: The anthropologist studies ancient tribes.
words.ex_cn: 这位人类学家研究古代部落。
words.en: An anthropologist is a person who studies anthropology, which is the study of human societies and cultures and their development.

words.ex: The doctor gave me an antibiotic for my infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了抗菌素治疗感染。
words.en: A substance that can kill or inhibit the growth of bacteria and other microorganisms.

words.ex: The doctor gave me antibiotics for my infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了抗生素来治疗感染。
words.en: Antibiotics are medicines that are used to treat infections caused by bacteria.

words.ex: The body makes an antibody to fight the virus.
words.ex_cn: 身体产生一种抗体来对抗病毒。
words.en: An antibody is a protein produced by the body's immune system when it detects harmful substances, called antigens. Each type of antibody is unique and defends the body against one specific type of antigen.

words.ex: I anticipate rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我预料明天会下雨。
words.en: If you anticipate an event, you realize in advance that it may happen and you are prepared for it.

words.ex: He adds antifreeze to the car in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他在冬天给汽车加防冻液。
words.en: A substance added to a liquid to lower its freezing point, used especially in the radiator of a motor vehicle.

words.ex: The old computer is antiquated and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧电脑过时且缓慢。
words.en: Something that is antiquated is old-fashioned or outdated and no longer suitable for modern conditions or purposes.

words.tr:
adj. 古老的；
n. 古董；
words.ex: He bought an antique chair from the old market.
words.ex_cn: 他从旧市场买了一把古老的椅子。
words.en: Something that is antique is old and often valuable because it is rare or well made.

words.ex: The ruins show the antiquity of this civilization.
words.ex_cn: 这些废墟展示了这个文明的古老。
words.en: The ancient past, especially the period before the Middle Ages.

words.tr: adj. 反托拉斯的；反垄断的
words.ex: The government filed an antitrust case against the big company.
words.ex_cn: 政府对该大公司提起了反垄断诉讼。
words.en: Relating to legislation or actions intended to prevent or control monopolies and promote competition.

words.tr: adj. 不定期的；非周期性的
words.ex: The aperiodic fluctuations in the stock market are hard to predict.
words.ex_cn: 股市中不定期的波动很难预测。
words.en: Not occurring at regular intervals; not periodic.

words.ex: The apex of the mountain is covered with snow.
words.ex_cn: 山的最高点被雪覆盖。
words.en: The highest point or top of something; the climax or culmination of something.

words.ex: They paid five dollars apiece for the tickets.
words.ex_cn: 他们每人五美元买了票。
words.en: If something is given or sold apiece, each person is given or sold one, or each thing is sold for a particular amount.

words.ex: The lab has a new apparatus for measuring temperature.
words.ex_cn: 实验室有一台新的温度测量装置。
words.en: The complex structure of a particular system or organization, or the equipment used for a specific purpose.

words.ex: She bought new apparel for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了新衣服。
words.en: Clothing, especially outer garments; attire.

words.ex: It is apparent that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is apparent, it seems to be true, although you cannot be certain that it is.

words.tr:
n. 吸引力；上诉；
v. 吸引；诉请；呼吁；
words.ex: The appeal of the beach drew many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 海滩的吸引力吸引了许多游客。
words.en: If you appeal to someone to do something, you make a serious and urgent request to them. If you appeal against a decision or sentence, you formally ask a court or other authority to change it. If something appeals to you, you like it or it interests you.

words.ex: He has appendicitis and needs surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他得了阑尾炎，需要手术。
words.en: Appendicitis is a medical condition in which the appendix becomes inflamed and painful, often requiring surgery to remove the appendix.

words.ex: He has an appetite for spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢辛辣食物。
words.en: A desire or liking for something, especially food.

words.ex: The kitchen has a new washing appliance.
words.ex_cn: 厨房里有一台新的洗衣机。
words.en: An appliance is a device or machine that is used to perform a particular task, especially in the home.

words.ex: This rule is applicable to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If something is applicable to a particular situation, it is relevant or suitable for that situation.

words.ex: The boss appointed Tom as the new manager.
words.ex_cn: 老板任命汤姆为新经理。
words.en: If you appoint someone to a job or official position, you formally choose them for it.

words.ex: The teacher apportioned the books equally among the students.
words.ex_cn: 老师把书平均分给了学生们。
words.en: To apportion something is to divide it and share it out among several people or things.

words.ex: He is an apprentice in a car repair shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是汽车修理店的一名学徒。
words.en: An apprentice is a young person who works for someone in order to learn their skill.

words.ex: He completed his apprenticeship as a carpenter.
words.ex_cn: 他完成了木工学徒期。
words.en: An apprenticeship is a period of time in which someone learns a trade or profession by working under the supervision of a skilled worker.

words.ex: His work finally received the approbation of his peers.
words.ex_cn: 他的工作最终得到了同行的认可。
words.en: Official approval or agreement.

words.tr: adj. 适当的；合适的；恰当的；
words.ex: This dress is appropriate for a wedding.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子适合参加婚礼。
words.en: Something that is appropriate is suitable or acceptable for a particular situation.

words.tr: n. 拨用；拨款；挪用；占有
words.ex: The government made an appropriation for education.
words.ex_cn: 政府为教育拨款。
words.en: The act of setting something aside for a specific purpose, especially funds.

words.ex: The teacher gave her approval for the project.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这个项目表示了赞成。
words.en: If you give your approval to something, you agree with it or allow it to happen.

words.tr: v. 批准；认可；通过；赞成(连of)
words.ex: My mom will approve my new phone.
words.ex_cn: 我妈妈会同意我买新手机。
words.en: If you approve of an action, event, or suggestion, you like it or are pleased about it.

words.tr:
adj. 近似的；大约的；
v. 接近；
words.ex: The approximate cost is $50.
words.ex_cn: 费用大约是50美元。
words.en: An approximate number, time, or position is close to the correct number, time, or position, but is not exact.

words.tr: n. 水族馆；水族箱；养鱼缸；
words.ex: We visited the aquarium to see the fish.
words.ex_cn: 我们去水族馆看鱼。
words.en: A tank or building in which fish and other water creatures and plants are kept.

words.tr: adj. 水生的；水栖的；水中的；
words.ex: The fish live in aquatic plants.
words.ex_cn: 这些鱼生活在水生植物中。
words.en: Relating to water; living in or near water or taking place in water.

words.ex: The land is arable and good for growing wheat.
words.ex_cn: 这块地是可耕的，适合种植小麦。
words.en: Arable land is land that is suitable for growing crops.

words.ex: The teacher chose an arbitrary number to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师随意选了一个数字来开始游戏。
words.en: If you describe an action, rule, or decision as arbitrary, you think that it is not based on any principle, plan, or system. It often seems unfair because of this.

words.ex: The arboreal squirrel climbs high in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 这种树栖松鼠在高高的树上攀爬。
words.en: Relating to trees; living in trees.

words.ex: The bridge has a stone arch.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥有一个石拱。
words.en: An arch is a structure that is curved at the top and is usually made of stone or brick. Arches are often used to support the weight of a bridge or the roof of a building.

words.ex: They found an archaeological site near the river.
words.ex_cn: 他们在河边发现了一个考古遗址。
words.en: Relating to the study of human history and prehistory through the excavation of sites and the analysis of artifacts and other physical remains.

words.ex: The archaeologist found an old pot in the ground.
words.ex_cn: 这位考古学家在地下发现了一个旧陶罐。
words.en: An archaeologist is someone who studies the societies and cultures of the past by examining the remains of their buildings, tools, and other objects.

words.ex: He loves archaeology and digs old artifacts.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱考古学，挖掘古代文物。
words.en: Archaeology is the study of the societies and peoples of the past by examining the remains of their buildings, tools, and other objects.

words.tr: n. 主要敌人，大敌；撒旦，魔王
words.ex: The superhero's archenemy was a powerful villain with a personal vendetta.
words.ex_cn: 这位超级英雄的主要敌人是一个有着私人恩怨的强大反派。
words.en: An archenemy is the main enemy of someone or something, often portrayed as a formidable opponent.

words.ex: He is an architect who designs houses.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位设计房屋的建筑师。
words.en: An architect is a person who designs buildings and advises in their construction.

words.ex: He is an ardent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: An ardent person has strong feelings or enthusiasm for something.

words.ex: The arid land has little rain and no trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片干旱的土地降雨稀少，没有树木。
words.en: An arid area of land has so little rain that it is very dry and cannot support much vegetation.

words.tr: n. 贵族政治；贵族统治；贵族
words.ex: The aristocracy lived in big castles long ago.
words.ex_cn: 很久以前，贵族住在巨大的城堡里。
words.en: The highest class in certain societies, especially those holding hereditary titles or offices.

words.ex: He does arithmetic every day with his little sister.
words.ex_cn: 他每天和妹妹一起做算术。
words.en: Arithmetic is the part of mathematics that deals with the addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of numbers.

words.ex: There was an array of people at the concert.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会上人山人海。
words.en: An array of different things or people is a large number or wide range of them.

words.ex: The police arrested the thief last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚逮捕了那个小偷。
words.en: If the police arrest you, they take charge of you and take you to a police station, because they believe you may have committed a crime.

words.ex: The artery carries blood from the heart.
words.ex_cn: 动脉将血液从心脏输送到身体。
words.en: An artery is a tube that carries blood from the heart to the rest of the body.

words.ex: He has arthritis in his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他双手有关节炎。
words.en: Arthritis is a medical condition in which the joints in someone's body are swollen and painful.

words.ex: He can articulate his ideas clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: If you describe someone as articulate, you mean that they are able to express their thoughts and ideas easily and clearly.

words.tr: n. 人工制品；手工艺品；加工品
words.ex: The museum has an ancient artifact.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆里有一件古代文物。
words.en: An artifact is an object that is made by a person, especially something of historical or cultural interest.

words.ex: His aspiration is to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他的渴望是成为一名医生。
words.en: A strong desire to achieve something high or great.

words.ex: He will assemble the toy for his son.
words.ex_cn: 他将为儿子组装玩具。
words.en: If people assemble or if someone assembles them, they come together in a group, usually for a particular purpose such as a meeting.

words.tr: n. 汇编程序；汇编机；装配工
words.ex: The programmer wrote code for the assembler.
words.ex_cn: 程序员为汇编程序编写了代码。
words.en: An assembler is a type of computer program that interprets software programs written in assembly language into machine language, code, and instructions that can be executed by a computer.

words.tr: v. 断言；宣称；坚持；维护
words.ex: He asserts that the answer is correct.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持认为答案是正确的。
words.en: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.

words.ex: His assertion was simple: the project will finish on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的断言很简单：项目会按时完成。
words.en: A statement that is made with confidence but without proof.

words.ex: The teacher will assess your homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会评估你的作业。
words.en: to judge or decide the amount, value, quality, or importance of something

words.tr: n. 有价值的人或物；长处；
words.ex: He is an asset to the team because he works hard.
words.ex_cn: 他是个有价值的人，因为他工作努力。
words.en: An asset is something valuable that an individual, corporation, or country owns or controls with the expectation that it will provide a future benefit.

words.ex: The teacher will assign homework today.
words.ex_cn: 老师今天会布置作业。
words.en: To give someone a particular job or task; to allocate a resource or responsibility to a particular person or purpose.

words.ex: He assists his brother with homework.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助弟弟做作业。
words.en: If you assist someone, you help them to do a job or task by doing part of the work for them.

words.tr:
v. 把…联系在一起；
adj. 副的；
n. 同事；伙伴；
words.ex: He associates happiness with family time.
words.ex_cn: 他把幸福与家庭时光联系在一起。
words.en: If you associate someone or something with a particular quality or idea, or if they are associated with it, you connect them in your mind with that quality or idea.

words.ex: He joined a local book association.
words.ex_cn: 他加入了一个本地的图书协会。
words.en: An association is an official group of people who have the same job, aim, or interest.

words.ex: I assume it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假定明天会下雨。
words.en: If you assume that something is true, you accept that it is true without proof.

words.ex: His assumption was that the train would be on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是火车会准时。
words.en: An assumption is something that you assume to be the case, even without proof.

words.ex: The asteroid flew past Earth safely.
words.ex_cn: 这颗小行星安全地从地球旁飞过。
words.en: An asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the sun. Large numbers of these, ranging enormously in size, are found between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter, though some have more eccentric orbits.

words.ex: He has asthma and cannot run fast.
words.ex_cn: 他有哮喘，不能跑快。
words.en: A respiratory condition marked by spasms in the bronchi of the lungs, causing difficulty in breathing. It usually results from an allergic reaction or other forms of hypersensitivity.

words.ex: He uses an astronomical telescope to watch stars.
words.ex_cn: 他用一架天文望远镜观察星星。
words.en: If you describe an amount, especially the cost of something as astronomical, you are emphasizing that it is very large indeed.

words.ex: He loves watching stars and learning astronomy.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢看星星并学习天文学。
words.en: Astronomy is the scientific study of celestial objects, space, and the physical universe as a whole.

words.ex: The atmosphere keeps the Earth warm.
words.ex_cn: 大气使地球保持温暖。
words.en: The atmosphere is the layer of gases surrounding a planet or other material body, held in place by the gravity of the body.

words.ex: He worked hard to attain his goals.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以达到他的目标。
words.en: If you attain something, you gain it or achieve it, often after a lot of effort.

words.tr:
n. 企图；试图；
v. 企图；试图；
words.ex: His attempt to cheat on the test failed.
words.ex_cn: 他企图在考试中作弊，但失败了。
words.en: To make an effort to achieve or complete something, especially something difficult.

words.ex: His attendance at the meeting was mandatory.
words.ex_cn: 他必须出席这次会议。
words.en: The act of being present at a place or event.

words.ex: The attendee listened carefully to the speaker.
words.ex_cn: 与会者认真听演讲者讲话。
words.en: An attendee is a person who is present at an event, meeting, or function.

words.tr: n. 律师；辩护律师；代理人
words.ex: The attorney helped the man with his case.
words.ex_cn: 律师帮助那个人处理了他的案件。
words.en: An attorney is a lawyer who is qualified to represent a client in court.

words.ex: The attraction of the city draws many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的吸引力吸引了许多游客。
words.en: An attraction is something that makes people want to go to a place or do a particular thing because they are interested in it.

words.ex: The accident is attributable to poor road conditions.
words.ex_cn: 这起事故可归因于糟糕的路况。
words.en: Capable of being attributed to someone or something.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.ex: The attrition between the two rocks caused sparks.
words.ex_cn: 两块岩石之间的摩擦产生了火花。
words.en: Attrition refers to the process of reducing something's strength or effectiveness through sustained attack or pressure, or the gradual reduction in the number of employees in an organization by retirement, resignation, or death.

words.ex: The old painting was sold at an auction.
words.ex_cn: 那幅旧画在拍卖会上被卖出了。
words.en: An auction is a public sale where goods or property are sold to the highest bidder.

words.tr: n. 高保真音响爱好者
words.ex: He spent a fortune on his audiophile equipment.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的高保真音响设备花了一大笔钱。
words.en: An audiophile is a person who is enthusiastic about high-fidelity sound reproduction.

words.ex: The company hired an expert to do an audit.
words.ex_cn: 公司聘请了一位专家进行审计。
words.en: An audit is an official examination of the accounts of a business or organization to check that they are accurate and correct.

words.ex: The school concert was held in the auditorium.
words.ex_cn: 学校的音乐会是在礼堂举行的。
words.en: An auditorium is the part of a theatre, concert hall, or other public building in which the audience sits.

words.ex: The old house has a mysterious aura.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子有一种神秘的氛围。
words.en: An aura is a distinctive atmosphere or quality that seems to surround and be generated by a person, thing, or place.

words.ex: She saw the aurora in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 她在夜空中看到了极光。
words.en: An aurora is a natural light display in the sky, predominantly seen in the high latitude (Arctic and Antarctic) regions, caused by the collision of solar wind and magnetospheric charged particles with the high altitude atmosphere.

words.tr: adj. 简朴的；严厉的；苦行的；紧缩的
words.ex: The room has austere walls with no decorations.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的墙壁朴素，没有任何装饰。
words.en: If you describe something as austere, you approve of its plain and simple appearance.

words.tr: adj. 真正的；真实的；真迹的；可靠的；
words.ex: This is an authentic painting by Picasso.
words.ex_cn: 这是一幅毕加索的真迹。
words.en: If something is authentic, it is real, true, or what people say it is.

words.tr: v. 证明…是真实的；鉴别
words.ex: He must authenticate his identity with a password.
words.ex_cn: 他必须用密码验证自己的身份。
words.en: To authenticate something means to prove or confirm that it is genuine or true.

words.ex: The teacher gave an authoritative answer.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了一个权威性的回答。
words.en: If something is authoritative, it is respected and accepted as true or correct because it comes from a reliable source.

words.tr: n. 权威；官方机构；权力；权威人士；当局；
words.ex: The teacher is an authority on ancient history.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师是古代史方面的权威。
words.en: The power to make decisions or enforce rules.

words.ex: The manager will authorize the payment tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 经理明天将批准这笔付款。
words.en: To give official permission for something to happen, or to give someone official permission to do something.

words.ex: He wrote his autobiography when he was 70.
words.ex_cn: 他70岁时写了自传。
words.en: An autobiography is a book about the life of a person, written by that person.

words.ex: The factory will automate the assembly line.
words.ex_cn: 工厂将自动化装配线。
words.en: To automate a factory, office, or industrial process means to put in machines which can do the work instead of people.

words.ex: The door opens automatically when you get close.
words.ex_cn: 当你靠近时，门会自动打开。
words.en: If something happens automatically, it happens as a part of the normal process or system, without needing to be started by someone.

words.ex: The factory uses automation to make cars.
words.ex_cn: 工厂使用自动化来制造汽车。
words.en: The use of largely automatic equipment in a system of manufacturing or other production process.

words.ex: He drives an automobile to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天开车去上班。
words.en: A vehicle that is powered by an engine and is used for carrying passengers on roads.

words.tr: n. 自主权；自治权；自治；
words.ex: The region demands autonomy from the central government.
words.ex_cn: 该地区要求从中央政府获得自主权。
words.en: Autonomy is the ability or condition of being self-governing; independence in one's thoughts or actions.

words.ex: The availability of free Wi-Fi is important for travelers.
words.ex_cn: 免费Wi-Fi的可用性对旅行者很重要。
words.en: The quality of being able to be used or obtained.

words.ex: Applications arrived in an avalanche after the job posting.
words.ex_cn: 职位发布后，申请纷至沓来。
words.en: An avalanche is a large mass of snow, ice, and rocks that falls quickly down the side of a mountain.

words.ex: He has an aversion to spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他厌恶辛辣食物。
words.en: A strong dislike or disinclination towards someone or something.

words.ex: The avian species flew south for winter.
words.ex_cn: 这种鸟类飞往南方过冬。
words.en: Relating to birds.

words.tr: n. 航空；航空学；飞行（术）；
words.ex: He works in aviation as a pilot.
words.ex_cn: 他作为一名飞行员从事航空工作。
words.en: Aviation is the operation and production of aircraft.

words.tr: n. 飞行员；飞机驾驶员
words.ex: The aviator flew a plane over the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员驾机飞越了山脉。
words.en: An aviator is a person who flies an aircraft.

words.ex: He avidly ate the last cookie.
words.ex_cn: 他贪心地吃掉了最后一块饼干。
words.en: If you do something avidly, you do it eagerly and enthusiastically.

words.ex: He avoids eating sugar to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他避免吃糖以保持健康。
words.en: If you avoid something, you take action in order to prevent it from happening to you.

words.ex: The village is a backwater with no modern facilities.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄是个穷乡僻壤，没有现代设施。
words.en: A backwater is a part of a river where the water is stagnant or moves very slowly, or a place that is isolated and not influenced by new ideas or events.

words.ex: The bacterium causes sickness in humans.
words.ex_cn: 这种细菌会导致人类生病。
words.en: A bacterium is a very small organism which often causes disease.

words.ex: He drinks coffee on the balcony every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都在阳台上喝咖啡。
words.en: A balcony is a platform on the outside of a building, enclosed by walls or balustrades, supported by columns or console brackets. The platform is projected from the wall of a building, usually above the ground floor.

words.ex: The missile is ballistic and travels far.
words.ex_cn: 这枚导弹是弹道的，能飞得很远。
words.en: relating to the study of the dynamics of projectiles

words.tr: n. 破产；倒闭；无偿付能力
words.ex: The company filed for bankruptcy last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司去年申请了破产。
words.en: Bankruptcy is a legal status of a person or other entity that cannot repay the debts it owes to creditors.

words.tr: n. 条状物；酒吧；栅栏；棒；
words.ex: He ate a chocolate bar after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后吃了一条巧克力。
words.en: A bar is a place where alcoholic drinks are served, or a long, narrow piece of metal or wood used for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The fish has a sharp barb on its tail.
words.ex_cn: 这条鱼的尾巴上有一个尖锐的倒刺。
words.en: A barb is a sharp projection near the end of an arrow, fishhook, or similar object, which is angled away from the main point so as to make extraction difficult. It can also refer to a remark that is meant to hurt someone's feelings.

words.tr:
n. 树皮；
v. 狗吠；
words.ex: The dog climbed the tree and touched the bark.
words.ex_cn: 狗爬上了树，摸了摸树皮。
words.en: The sound a dog makes; the outer covering of a tree.

words.tr: n. 营房；兵营；（一片）简陋的大房子
words.ex: The soldiers live in the barracks near the base.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们住在基地附近的兵营里。
words.en: A barracks is a building or group of buildings where soldiers live.

words.ex: He poured water into a wooden barrel.
words.ex_cn: 他把水倒进一个木桶里。
words.en: A barrel is a large, round container for liquids or food, typically made of wood or metal.

words.ex: The barren land cannot grow any crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片贫瘠的土地无法种植任何庄稼。
words.en: If you describe something as barren, you mean that it is not able to produce anything, especially plants or crops.

words.ex: The fence is a barrier to animals.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏是动物的障碍。
words.en: A barrier is something such as a rule, law, or policy that makes it difficult or impossible for something to happen or be achieved.

words.ex: The bakery made a new batch of bread this morning.
words.ex_cn: 这家面包店今天早上做了一批新面包。
words.en: A batch is a quantity or consignment of goods produced at one time.

words.ex: The battalion marched slowly through the town.
words.ex_cn: 那个营缓缓穿过小镇。
words.en: A battalion is a large group of soldiers that consists of three or more companies.

words.ex: She threaded a bead onto the string.
words.ex_cn: 她把一颗有孔的小珠穿在绳子上。
words.en: A bead is a small piece of glass, wood, or plastic that is used for decorating clothes or making jewellery.

words.ex: The satellite beams signals to Earth.
words.ex_cn: 卫星向地球发射信号。
words.en: A beam is a long, thick piece of wood, metal, or concrete that is used to support the roof of a building. It can also refer to a line of light that shines from a bright object, or a smile that shows someone is very happy.

words.ex: The bearer of the ticket can enter the concert.
words.ex_cn: 票的持有人可以进入音乐会。
words.en: A bearer is someone who carries or holds something, especially a document or message, or someone who is entitled to receive something, such as a check or a ticket.

words.tr: v. 招手示意；举手召唤；引诱
words.ex: He beckoned to the boy to come closer.
words.ex_cn: 他向那个男孩招手示意过来。
words.en: If you beckon to someone, you signal to them to come to you, usually by a gesture of your hand.

words.tr: n. 蜂窝；蜂箱；嘈杂的场所
words.ex: The bees live in a beehive near the garden.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂住在花园附近的一个蜂箱里。
words.en: A beehive is a structure in which bees are kept, which is designed to protect them from the weather and predators, and to provide them with a place to store honey.

words.ex: His behavioral changes worried his parents.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为变化让他的父母担心。
words.en: Relating to the way in which someone behaves.

words.tr:
n. 风箱（复数名词）
v. 怒吼；吼叫；咆哮；“bellow”的第三人称单数
n. 咆哮；怒号；“bellow”的复数
words.ex: The blacksmith pulled the bellows to make the fire hotter.
words.ex_cn: 铁匠拉风箱让火更旺。
words.en: A bellows is a device for producing a strong current of air, used especially for blowing a fire.

words.ex: This test is a benchmark for all students.
words.ex_cn: 这个测试是所有学生的标准。
words.en: A benchmark is something whose quality or quantity is known and which can therefore be used as a standard with which other things can be compared.

words.tr: n. 恩人；捐助者；赠送者
words.ex: The benefactor gave money to the school.
words.ex_cn: 资助人捐钱给学校。
words.en: A benefactor is a person who gives money or other help to a person or cause.

words.ex: He is the beneficiary of his father's will.
words.ex_cn: 他是他父亲遗嘱的受益人。
words.en: A beneficiary is someone who receives money or other benefits as a result of something, especially a will or insurance policy.

words.tr:
v. 有益于；有助于；
n. 利益；好处；
words.ex: Exercise benefits your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼有益于你的健康。
words.en: A benefit is something that helps you or improves your life in some way.

words.ex: His benevolence helped the poor family.
words.ex_cn: 他的仁慈帮助了这个贫困家庭。
words.en: The quality of being well meaning; kindness.

words.ex: The king will bestow a medal on the hero.
words.ex_cn: 国王将把奖章授予这位英雄。
words.en: To bestow something on someone means to give or present it to them.

words.ex: He felt deep pain from his friend's betrayal.
words.ex_cn: 他因朋友的背叛感到深深的痛苦。
words.en: The action of betraying one's country, a group, or a person; treachery.

words.tr: adj. 较富裕的；境况较好的
words.ex: The better-off families can afford private schools.
words.ex_cn: 条件较好的家庭能负担得起私立学校。
words.en: In a more favorable position, especially in financial terms.

words.ex: He drinks a cold beverage after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后喝一杯冷饮。
words.en: A drink, especially one other than water; a liquid for drinking.

words.ex: The teacher showed a bias for students who arrived early.
words.ex_cn: 老师对早到的学生有偏爱。
words.en: If someone is biased, they prefer one group of people to another, and behave unfairly as a result.

words.tr:
v. 斗嘴；闪烁
n. 口角
words.ex: They bicker over small things every day.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天为小事争吵。
words.en: If people bicker, they argue or quarrel about unimportant things.

words.tr:
n. 努力争取；出价；投标；
v. 出价；投标；
words.ex: His bid for the championship inspired everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他为冠军所做的努力鼓舞了所有人。
words.en: To bid means to offer a particular amount of money for something that is being sold, especially at an auction, or to offer to do work or provide services for a particular price.

words.ex: The river reaches a bifurcation where it splits into two streams.
words.ex_cn: 河流到达一个分叉点，分为两条支流。
words.en: The division of something into two branches or parts.

words.ex: The two countries signed a bilateral agreement.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项双边协议。
words.en: Involving or affecting two parties, countries, etc.

words.tr: n. 演员表；演员次序；营业额
words.ex: The billing at the end of the movie listed all the actors.
words.ex_cn: 电影结尾的演员表列出了所有演员。
words.en: The process of preparing and sending invoices to customers for goods or services provided.

words.ex: He bind the books with string.
words.ex_cn: 他用绳子把书捆起来。
words.en: To tie something or someone tightly or to fasten something.

words.ex: The bag is biodegradable.
words.ex_cn: 这个袋子是可生物降解的。
words.en: A substance or chemical that is biodegradable can be decomposed by bacteria or other living organisms, and therefore does not pollute the environment.

words.ex: She is a bioengineer who specializes in tissue regeneration.
words.ex_cn: 她是一名专注于组织再生的生物工程师。
words.en: A bioengineer is a person who applies engineering principles to biological systems and biomedical technologies.

words.ex: He read a biography of Nelson Mandela.
words.ex_cn: 他读了一本关于纳尔逊·曼德拉的传记。
words.en: A biography is a detailed description of a person's life. It involves more than just the basic facts like education, work, relationships, and death; it portrays a person's experience of these life events.

words.ex: He works in biomedical research at the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他在医院从事生物医学研究。
words.en: Relating to both biology and medicine, especially in the application of biological principles to medical research or practice.

words.ex: The biophysicist studied the molecular interactions in cells.
words.ex_cn: 这位生物物理学家研究了细胞中的分子相互作用。
words.en: A biophysicist is a scientist who applies the theories and methods of physics to understand biological systems.

words.ex: The biosphere includes all living things on Earth.
words.ex_cn: 生物圈包括地球上所有生物。
words.en: The biosphere is the part of the Earth's surface and atmosphere in which plants and animals can live.

words.ex: The line bisects the angle into two equal parts.
words.ex_cn: 这条线将角平分为两个相等的部分。
words.en: To divide something into two equal parts.

words.tr: adj. 离奇的；奇特的；奇怪的；
words.ex: The clown wore a bizarre hat with three eyes.
words.ex_cn: 小丑戴着一顶有三只眼睛的离奇帽子。
words.en: Something that is bizarre is very odd and strange.

words.ex: The city had a blackout during the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争期间，这座城市实行了灯火管制。
words.en: A blackout is a period of time during which there is no electricity, or when the lights are turned off, especially as a result of an emergency or for a theatrical effect. It can also refer to a temporary loss of memory or consciousness.

words.ex: The soup was too bland for me.
words.ex_cn: 这汤太淡了，我不喜欢。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as bland, you mean that they are rather dull and unexciting.

words.tr: n. 一阵强劲的气流；爆炸；
words.ex: A blast of cold wind hit the window.
words.ex_cn: 一阵冷风击中了窗户。
words.en: A blast is a sudden loud noise or a strong gust of wind. It can also refer to an explosion or the act of blowing something up. As a verb, it means to explode or to criticize severely.

words.ex: The two countries are in the same bloc.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家属于同一个集团。
words.en: A bloc is a group of countries or parties with similar political interests, especially when they act together in international affairs.

words.tr:
n. 大楼；大厦；块；街区；障碍物；
v. 阻塞；阻碍；
words.ex: The new block is next to the park.
words.ex_cn: 这栋新大楼就在公园旁边。
words.en: A block is a large solid piece of material with flat surfaces on each side. As a verb, to block means to prevent movement or progress.

words.ex: The ink blot ruined his homework.
words.ex_cn: 墨水污点弄脏了他的作业。
words.en: A blot is a mark or stain that spoils the appearance of something. It can also refer to an act that damages someone's reputation.

words.tr: n. 蓝莓音乐或蓝草音乐；莓系属的牧草
words.ex: He plays the banjo in a bluegrass band.
words.ex_cn: 他在一支蓝草音乐乐队中弹奏班卓琴。
words.en: Bluegrass is a style of American country music that originated in the southern United States, characterized by its use of acoustic stringed instruments and a fast tempo.

words.ex: He bluntly said he did not like the food.
words.ex_cn: 他直率地说他不喜欢这食物。
words.en: If you say something bluntly, you say it very directly, without trying to be polite or to hide unpleasant facts.

words.ex: The boarder eats dinner with the family.
words.ex_cn: 这个寄宿生和家人一起吃晚饭。
words.en: A boarder is someone who pays to live and receive meals in someone else's house, or a student who lives at school during the term.

words.tr: n. 公寓；寄宿公寓；供膳寄宿舍
words.ex: She lives in a boardinghouse near the school.
words.ex_cn: 她住在学校附近的一栋公寓里。
words.en: A boardinghouse is a house where people pay to stay and receive meals.

words.ex: He gave a bold speech in front of the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前发表了大胆的演讲。
words.en: Someone who is bold is not afraid to do things which involve risk or danger.

words.ex: Exercise can bolster your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的健康。
words.en: If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it. A bolster is also a long, firm pillow.

words.ex: The mechanic tightened the bolt with a wrench.
words.ex_cn: 机械师用扳手拧紧了螺栓。
words.en: A bolt is a type of fastener consisting of a threaded pin or rod with a head at one end, designed to be inserted through holes in assembled parts and tightened by a nut from the other end. It can also refer to a sudden dash or run, or to eat food quickly and without chewing.

words.ex: The soldiers were bombarded with cannon fire.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们遭到炮火轰击。
words.en: To bombard someone or something means to attack them continuously with bombs, shells, or other missiles. It can also mean to subject someone to a lot of something, such as questions or information.

words.ex: He is a bona fide expert in history.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位真正的历史专家。
words.en: Made in good faith without fraud or deceit.

words.tr:
n. 纽带；联系；债券；保释金；协定
v. （使）黏合；相互联结
words.ex: Family is the bond that keeps us together.
words.ex_cn: 家庭是我们团结的纽带。
words.en: A bond between people is a strong feeling of friendship, love, or shared beliefs and experiences that unites them.

words.tr: n. 奖金；红利；额外津贴；
words.ex: He received a bonus for working overtime.
words.ex_cn: 他因加班获得了奖金。
words.en: A bonus is an extra amount of money that is added to someone's pay, usually because they have worked very hard.

words.ex: The city had an economic boom after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 新工厂开业后，这座城市迎来了经济繁荣。
words.en: If there is a boom in the economy, there is an increase in economic activity, for example in the amount of things that are being bought and sold.

words.tr:
n. 飞去来器；回旋镖；回力镖
v. 自食其果；害人反害己
words.ex: He threw the boomerang and it came back to him.
words.ex_cn: 他扔出了回旋镖，它又飞回到他身边。
words.en: A boomerang is a curved piece of wood which comes back to you if you throw it correctly. It is used by Australian Aborigines for hunting and for sport.

words.tr:
v. 促进；使增长；
n. 提高；增强；
words.ex: Exercise can boost your energy.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进你的精力。
words.en: If one thing boosts another, it causes it to increase, improve, or be more successful.

words.ex: He bought a hot dog from a food booth.
words.ex_cn: 他从一个小吃亭买了个热狗。
words.en: A booth is a small area separated from a larger public area by screens or thin walls where, for example, people can make a phone call or vote in private.

words.ex: The boreal forest is cold and full of pine trees.
words.ex_cn: 北方森林寒冷且长满松树。
words.en: Of or relating to the north or the north wind.

words.tr:
n. 弹跳；跳动；
v. 弹跳；反弹；
words.ex: The ball had a high bounce on the concrete.
words.ex_cn: 球在混凝土上弹跳得很高。
words.en: If something bounces or if you bounce it, it moves away from a surface after hitting it.

words.tr: adj. 一定会；密切相关的；有义务的； v. “bind”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is bound to win the race.
words.ex_cn: 他一定会赢得比赛。
words.en: If one person, thing, or situation is bound to another, they are closely connected with each other, and it is difficult for them to be separated or to escape from each other. If you say that something is bound to happen, you mean that you are sure it will happen, because it is a natural consequence of something that is already known or exists.

words.ex: His bounty helped the poor family survive winter.
words.ex_cn: 他的慷慨帮助这个贫困家庭度过了冬天。
words.en: If you say that someone is bountiful or does something in a bountiful way, you mean that they are very generous or that they give a lot of something.

words.tr:
n. 中产阶级的人；资产阶级的人
adj. 中产阶级的；追求名利的；资产阶级的
words.ex: He lives a bourgeois life with a big house and a car.
words.ex_cn: 他过着资产阶级的生活，有一栋大房子和一辆车。
words.en: If you describe people, their way of life, or their attitudes as bourgeois, you are criticizing them for caring too much about money and possessions and for being too conventional.

words.ex: She sat under a bower of roses.
words.ex_cn: 她坐在一丛玫瑰花形成的凉亭下。
words.en: A bower is a pleasant place in the shade under a tree or a structure in a garden where people can sit and relax.

words.tr:
n. 抵制；拒绝参加；
v. 抵制；拒绝参加；
words.ex: The students organized a boycott of the unfair school rule.
words.ex_cn: 学生们组织了对这项不公平校规的抵制。
words.en: If a country, group, or person boycotts a country, organization, or activity, they refuse to be involved with it in any way because they disapprove of it.

words.tr:
n. 支撑物；支架；牙箍
v. 支撑；绷紧；紧靠；准备好
words.ex: The old bookshelf needs a brace to stay steady.
words.ex_cn: 旧书架需要一个支撑物来保持稳定。
words.en: To brace oneself means to prepare oneself for something difficult or unpleasant.

words.ex: He bought a brass lamp at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一个黄铜制品台灯。
words.en: Brass is a yellow-coloured metal made from copper and zinc. It is used especially for making ornaments and musical instruments.

words.tr:
v. 酿造；沏；酝酿
n. 酿造的饮料；啤酒
words.ex: He brews coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冲咖啡。
words.en: If you brew tea or coffee, you make it by pouring hot water over tea leaves or ground coffee. If you brew beer, you make it by soaking grain in water and then fermenting it.

words.ex: Hard work can bring about success.
words.ex_cn: 努力工作可以带来成功。
words.en: To cause something to happen.

words.ex: He picked up a brochure about the city.
words.ex_cn: 他拿了一本关于这座城市的宣传小册子。
words.en: A brochure is a type of small magazine or booklet containing pictures and information about something or advertising something.

words.ex: He brokered a deal between the two companies.
words.ex_cn: 他为两家公司安排了协商并达成协议。
words.en: A broker is a person whose job is to buy and sell shares, foreign money, or goods for other people.

words.tr: n. 经纪业务；经纪人佣金（或回扣）
words.ex: He works at a brokerage firm.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家经纪公司工作。
words.en: A brokerage is a company that buys and sells shares, bonds, and other investments for people and organizations.

words.ex: The statue is made of bronze.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像由青铜制成。
words.en: Bronze is a yellowish-brown metal which is a mixture of copper and tin.

words.ex: The storm caused a brutal flood that destroyed many homes.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴引发了残酷的洪水，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: A brutal act or person is cruel and violent.

words.ex: He filled the bucket with water from the well.
words.ex_cn: 他从井里打了一桶水。
words.en: A bucket is a round container with a handle, used for carrying liquids or other substances.

words.ex: He loves the bucolic life in the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢乡村的田园生活。
words.en: Relating to the pleasant aspects of the countryside and country life.

words.tr:
n. 预算；预算金额；
adj. 廉价的；花钱少的；
v. 为 ... 做预算；
words.ex: We made a budget for our vacation.
words.ex_cn: 我们为旅行制定了一个预算。
words.en: A budget is a plan that shows how much money a person or organization will earn and how much they will need or be able to spend.

words.ex: The budworm eats leaves on the trees.
words.ex_cn: 芽虫吃树上的叶子。
words.en: A budworm is the larva of a moth that feeds on the buds of plants, often causing significant damage to crops.

words.ex: The buffalo walks slowly across the grassland.
words.ex_cn: 水牛缓慢地走过草原。
words.en: A buffalo is a large animal of the cattle family, with long, curved horns. In North America, the buffalo is also called the bison.

words.ex: The computer uses a buffer to store data temporarily.
words.ex_cn: 计算机使用缓冲区临时存储数据。
words.en: A buffer is something that prevents something else from being harmed or that reduces the impact of something.

words.tr:
n. 膨胀；凸出部分；暴涨
v. 膨胀；凸出；急增
words.ex: The balloon begins to bulge when filled with air.
words.ex_cn: 气球充气时开始鼓起来。
words.en: If something bulges, it sticks out or swells in a rounded shape.

words.ex: The bulk of the students passed the exam.
words.ex_cn: 大部分学生通过了考试。
words.en: The bulk of something is most of it. The bulk of something is its size, especially when it is very large.

words.tr: adj. 有浮力的；心情愉快的；
words.ex: The buoyant life jacket keeps you on the water.
words.ex_cn: 有浮力的救生衣让你浮在水面上。
words.en: A buoyant object floats on a liquid or in the air. A buoyant economy, market, or industry is successful because a lot of money is being spent or invested in it.

words.ex: The heavy workload became a burden for her.
words.ex_cn: 繁重的工作量成了她的负担。
words.en: A burden is a heavy load that is difficult to carry, or a duty or responsibility that is hard to bear.

words.ex: The weather bureau issued a storm warning.
words.ex_cn: 气象局发布了风暴预警。
words.en: A bureau is an office, organization, or government department that collects and distributes information.

words.tr: vi. 夜盗；行窃; vt. 撬窃；行窃
words.ex: They tried to burglarize the house last night.
words.ex_cn: 他们昨晚试图闯入那所房子行窃。
words.en: To burglarize means to enter a building illegally and steal things.

words.tr:
v. 挖洞；钻进；翻寻
n. 地洞
words.ex: The rabbit burrows under the tree.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在树下打洞。
words.en: A burrow is a hole or tunnel dug by a small animal, such as a rabbit or a mole, as a dwelling. As a verb, to burrow means to dig a hole or tunnel for habitation or refuge.

words.ex: A butterfly is flying over the flowers.
words.ex_cn: 一只蝴蝶在花上飞舞。
words.en: A butterfly is an insect with large, often brightly coloured wings.

words.tr:
n. 扶墙；拱壁
v. 支持
words.ex: The old wall needs a buttress to stay standing.
words.ex_cn: 这面旧墙需要一个支撑物来保持不倒。
words.en: A buttress is a structure built against or projecting from a wall which serves to support or reinforce the wall. As a verb, to buttress means to support or strengthen something.

words.tr:
adj. 过去的
n. 过去的事
words.ex: He liked to talk about bygone days with his grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢和祖父谈论过去的时光。
words.en: Belonging to an earlier time.

words.tr: n. 规章制度；次要法规
words.ex: The town passed a new bylaw to stop littering.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇通过了一项新法规来禁止乱扔垃圾。
words.en: A bylaw is a rule or law established by an organization or community to regulate itself, as allowed or provided for by some higher authority.

words.ex: The sailors slept in the cabin during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 水手们在风暴期间睡在船舱里。
words.en: A cabin is a small room or compartment, especially one on a ship or an aircraft.

words.ex: He kept the dishes in the cabinet.
words.ex_cn: 他把盘子放在储藏柜里。
words.en: A cabinet is a piece of furniture with doors and shelves or drawers, used for storing or showing things. In politics, a cabinet is a group of people who are chosen by a head of state to give advice and to help set government policy.

words.ex: He drinks coffee to get caffeine.
words.ex_cn: 他喝咖啡来获取咖啡因。
words.en: A bitter alkaloid found in coffee and tea that is responsible for their stimulating effects.

words.tr: adj. 引起灾难的；遭受灾难的
words.ex: The storm caused a calamitous flood.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴造成了灾难性的洪水。
words.en: If you describe an event or situation as calamitous, you mean it is very unfortunate or serious.

words.ex: Milk has a lot of calcium.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶含有大量的钙。
words.en: A chemical element that is present in teeth and bones and is necessary for their health.

words.ex: He calculates the total cost quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速计算出总成本。
words.en: To determine by mathematical methods; compute.

words.tr: n. 微积分学；（人体内的）结石
words.ex: He is learning calculus at school.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学校学习微积分。
words.en: Calculus is a branch of mathematics that deals with the finding and properties of derivatives and integrals of functions, by methods originally based on the summation of infinitesimal differences.

words.tr: n. 加热；热污染（等于 thermal pollution）；温暖（的状态）
words.ex: The calefaction of the room made it warm.
words.ex_cn: 房间的加热使它变得温暖。
words.en: The process of heating or warming.

words.ex: He checks the calendar every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都看日历。
words.en: A calendar is a chart or device which displays the date and the day of the week, and often the whole of a particular year divided up into months, weeks, and days.

words.ex: The farmer feeds the calf every morning.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每天早上喂小牛。
words.en: A calf is a young cow or bull. It can also refer to the fleshy part of the back of the human leg below the knee.

words.ex: The caller asked for the manager.
words.ex_cn: 打电话者要求找经理。
words.en: A caller is someone who makes a telephone call or visits a place.

words.ex: He wrote the letter in calligraphic style.
words.ex_cn: 他用书法风格写了这封信。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by the art of beautiful handwriting.

words.tr: n. 摄像放像机；（便携式）摄像机
words.ex: He bought a camcorder to record his trip.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一个摄像机来记录他的旅行。
words.en: A camcorder is an electronic device that combines a video camera and a video recorder into one unit, typically used for recording video with sound.

words.tr: n. （政治、商业或社会性）活动；运动；
words.ex: The city launched a campaign to reduce plastic waste.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市发起了一项减少塑料垃圾的活动。
words.en: A campaign is a planned set of activities that people carry out over a period of time in order to achieve something such as social or political change.

words.ex: We set up our tent at the campsite near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 我们在湖边的野营地搭了帐篷。
words.en: A campsite is a place where people who are camping can stay, often with facilities such as toilets and showers.

words.ex: The canary sings beautifully in the cage.
words.ex_cn: 金丝雀在笼子里唱得非常动听。
words.en: A canary is a small yellow bird which is known for its singing.

words.ex: The canary sings beautifully in the cage.
words.ex_cn: 金丝雀在笼子里唱得非常动听。
words.en: A canary is a small yellow bird which is known for its singing.

words.tr:
n. 地毯
v. 在…上铺地毯；斥责；“carpet”的现在分词
words.ex: He laid new carpeting in the living room.
words.ex_cn: 他在客厅铺了新的地毯。
words.en: Carpeting refers to the material used for carpets or the act of covering a floor with carpet.

words.ex: The cartel controls the price of oil.
words.ex_cn: 这个卡特尔控制着石油的价格。
words.en: A cartel is an association of manufacturers or suppliers with the purpose of maintaining prices at a high level and restricting competition.

words.ex: A cascade of complaints flooded the office.
words.ex_cn: 大量投诉涌进了办公室。
words.en: A cascade is a small waterfall or a series of small waterfalls. As a verb, it means to flow or fall in or like a cascade.

words.tr: n. 个案总量；待处理案件之数量
words.ex: The social worker has a heavy caseload.
words.ex_cn: 这位社会工作者的工作负担很重。
words.en: The number of cases that a person or organization is responsible for dealing with at one time.

words.tr: n. 腰果（等于 cashew nut）；腰果树; adj. 漆树科的
words.ex: He eats a cashew every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃一颗腰果。
words.en: A cashew is a kidney-shaped nut that grows at the end of the cashew apple, which is the fruit of the cashew tree, native to northeastern Brazil.

words.ex: In some countries, caste determines a person's job and social status.
words.ex_cn: 在一些国家，社会等级决定一个人的职业和社会地位。
words.en: A caste is one of the traditional social classes into which people are divided in a Hindu society.

words.ex: The accident caused many casualties.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故造成了许多伤亡人员。
words.en: A casualty is a person who is killed or injured in a war or in an accident.

words.ex: The earthquake was a sudden cataclysm.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场突如其来的灾难。
words.en: A cataclysm is an event that causes great damage or makes a big change to something.

words.tr: adj. 灾难性的；大变动的
words.ex: The volcano erupted in a cataclysmic explosion.
words.ex_cn: 火山以一场灾难性的爆炸喷发了。
words.en: A cataclysmic event is one that causes great damage or suffering.

words.ex: He looked at the catalog to find the book.
words.ex_cn: 他翻看目录来找那本书。
words.en: A catalog is a list of things, such as the goods you can buy from a particular company, the objects in a museum, or the books in a library.

words.tr: phrase. 卡片目录（用于图书馆中按卡片索引图书的系统）
words.ex: He found the book using the card catalogue.
words.ex_cn: 他通过卡片目录找到了这本书。
words.en: A card catalogue is a system for organizing information about the books and other materials in a library, consisting of cards with information on them that are arranged in a particular order.

words.ex: The enzyme acts as a catalyst in the reaction.
words.ex_cn: 这种酶在反应中充当催化剂。
words.en: A catalyst is a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself undergoing any permanent chemical change. In a broader sense, it can also refer to a person or thing that precipitates a change.

words.ex: The catalytic converter reduces car pollution.
words.ex_cn: 催化转化器减少汽车污染。
words.en: Relating to or causing catalysis.

words.ex: The earthquake was a catastrophe.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场灾难。
words.en: An event causing great and often sudden damage or suffering; a disaster.

words.tr: adj. 绝对的；确定无疑的；分类的
words.ex: He gave a categorical no to the offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个提议给出了明确的拒绝。
words.en: If you are categorical about something, you state your views very definitely and firmly.

words.ex: This book belongs to the science category.
words.ex_cn: 这本书属于科学类别。
words.en: A category is a class or group of things that have similar characteristics.

words.ex: The restaurant caters to vegetarians.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅满足素食者的需求。
words.en: To cater means to provide food and drink at an event, often as a business service, or to provide what is needed or wanted by a particular person or group.

words.ex: The caterpillar is eating leaves on the tree.
words.ex_cn: 毛毛虫正在树上吃叶子。
words.en: A caterpillar is a small, worm-like animal that eventually develops into a butterfly or moth.

words.ex: The cathedral has tall towers and stained glass windows.
words.ex_cn: 这座大教堂有高高的塔楼和彩绘玻璃窗。
words.en: A cathedral is a very large and important church which has a bishop in charge of it.

words.tr:
n. 天主教徒；
adj. 天主教的；
words.ex: He is a catholic who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名每周日都去教堂的天主教徒。
words.en: If you describe a collection of things or people as catholic, you are emphasizing that it is varied and includes many different types of things or people.

words.tr: adj. 成为原因的，起因的；（语法）使役的; n. 使役动词
words.ex: The accident was causative of his injury.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故导致了他的受伤。
words.en: A causative factor is something that is responsible for an effect or result.

words.ex: The rain ceased after an hour.
words.ex_cn: 一小时后，雨停了。
words.en: If something ceases, it stops happening or existing.

words.tr: adj. 天空的；天体的；天国的；
words.ex: The celestial lights shone brightly in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 天空中的光芒在夜空中明亮地闪耀。
words.en: Relating to the sky or the heavens; belonging or relating to heaven as the abode of the gods.

words.ex: The cellular structure of plants is very small.
words.ex_cn: 植物的细胞结构非常微小。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of cells; having a porous structure.

words.tr:
v. 谴责；责难；指责
n. 谴责；责难；指责
words.ex: The teacher censured the student for cheating.
words.ex_cn: 老师谴责了那个作弊的学生。
words.en: If you censure someone for something that they have done, you tell them that you strongly disapprove of it.

words.ex: The government does a census every ten years.
words.ex_cn: 政府每十年进行一次人口普查。
words.en: A census is an official count or survey of a population, typically recording various details of individuals.

words.tr: n. 中心；向心性；集中性
words.ex: The centrality of the city makes it a key transportation hub.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的核心地位使其成为重要的交通枢纽。
words.en: The state or quality of being central, especially in importance or influence.

words.tr:
n. 陶瓷制品；陶瓷器；
adj. 陶质的；制陶的；
words.ex: He bought a ceramic bowl at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一个陶瓷碗。
words.en: Ceramic is a hard material that is made by baking clay or similar substances at high temperatures. It is used to make things such as tiles, dishes, and statues.

words.ex: He eats cereal with milk every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃谷类食品配牛奶。
words.en: A cereal is a grass that is cultivated for the edible components of its grain, composed of the endosperm, germ, and bran.

words.ex: He received a certificate for completing the course.
words.ex_cn: 他完成了课程后获得了证书。
words.en: A certificate is an official document attesting a fact, in particular.

words.ex: The doctor will certify that you are healthy.
words.ex_cn: 医生将证明你身体健康。
words.en: To officially declare something to be true, correct, or genuine, often in writing.

words.ex: He spoke with certitude about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他对于这个答案说话时充满确信。
words.en: A feeling of being certain or convinced about something.

words.ex: The cessation of rain allowed us to go outside.
words.ex_cn: 雨停了，我们就能出去了。
words.en: The fact or process of ending or being brought to an end.

words.tr: n. 一种轻马车（通常有车蓬，尤指单马双轮者）；（Chaise）（法）谢兹（人名）
words.ex: He rode in a chaise pulled by one horse.
words.ex_cn: 他乘坐一辆由一匹马拉的轻马车。
words.en: A chaise is a type of light, open carriage or a long chair for reclining.

words.ex: He drank wine from a golden chalice.
words.ex_cn: 他从一个金色酒杯里喝了葡萄酒。
words.en: A chalice is a large cup or goblet, typically made of gold or silver, used in religious ceremonies for drinking wine.

words.tr: n. 房间；室；腔；大会议室；
words.ex: He sat in the chamber and waited quietly.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在房间里安静地等待。
words.en: A chamber is a large room, especially one that is used for formal or public events.

words.tr: n. 性格；人物角色；特点；
words.ex: His character is kind and patient.
words.ex_cn: 他的性格善良且有耐心。
words.en: The combination of qualities or features that distinguishes one person, group, or thing from another.

words.tr: n. 特性描述；人物性格塑造；
words.ex: The characterization of the hero shows his bravery.
words.ex_cn: 对英雄的特性描述展现了他勇敢的品质。
words.en: The act of describing or representing the qualities or peculiarities of a person or thing.

words.ex: The charity helps poor children get food and education.
words.ex_cn: 这个慈善团体帮助贫困儿童获得食物和教育。
words.en: An organization that helps people in need, or the act of giving money, food, or help to those who need it.

words.ex: The teacher showed a chart of temperatures.
words.ex_cn: 老师展示了一张温度图表。
words.en: A chart is a graphical representation of data, in which the data is represented by symbols, such as bars in a bar chart, lines in a line chart, or slices in a pie chart.

words.ex: The Magna Carta is an old charter of rights.
words.ex_cn: 《大宪章》是一份古老的权力宪章。
words.en: A charter is a formal document describing the rights, aims, or principles of an organization or group of people.

words.ex: The birds made a soft chatter in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨鸟儿发出轻柔的啁啾声。
words.en: If you chatter, you talk quickly and continuously, usually about things which are not important.

words.tr: adj. 爱说话的；爱讲闲话的；饶舌的
words.ex: She is chatty during lunch break.
words.ex_cn: 她在午餐休息时很健谈。
words.en: If you describe someone as chatty, you mean that they enjoy talking in a friendly, informal way.

words.tr: n. 沙文主义；盲目的爱国心
words.ex: He shows chauvinism by thinking men are better than women.
