words.tr: n. 毕业文凭；学位证书；
words.ex: He received his diploma last June.
words.ex_cn: 他去年六月拿到了毕业文凭。
words.en: A diploma is a document which may be awarded by a university or college, or by a high school, showing that someone has successfully completed a course of study.

words.ex: He is a diplomatic ambassador who handles international relations.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位处理国际关系的外交大使。
words.en: Diplomatic means relating to diplomacy or diplomats, or using skill and tact in dealing with people.

words.ex: The weather was dire, with heavy rain and strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常可怕，下着大雨，刮着大风。
words.en: If you describe a situation as dire, you are emphasizing that it is very bad or serious.

words.tr: n. 伤残；失去能力；无能力；
words.ex: He has a disability that makes walking difficult.
words.ex_cn: 他有伤残，导致行走困难。
words.en: A disability is a physical or mental condition that limits a person's movements, senses, or activities.

words.ex: The earthquake caused a big disaster.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了一场大灾难。
words.en: A disaster is an unexpected event causing great damage, destruction, or distress.

words.ex: He decided to discard his old habits.
words.ex_cn: 他决定抛开旧习惯。
words.en: To discard something means to get rid of it because you no longer want it or need it.

words.ex: He could discern a small bird in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 他能辨明树上有一只小鸟。
words.en: If you can discern something, you are aware of it and know what it is.

words.tr:
v. 放电；放出；
n. 排放；
words.ex: The battery will discharge if left unused for a long time.
words.ex_cn: 如果长时间不使用，电池会放电。
words.en: If someone is discharged from a hospital, prison, or the armed forces, they are officially allowed to leave, or told that they must leave. If something is discharged from inside a place, it comes out.

words.ex: He was a faithful disciple of the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他是老师的一名忠实弟子。
words.en: A disciple is a follower or student of a teacher, leader, or philosopher.

words.tr:
n. 纪律；学科；科目；训练；惩戒；
v. 约束自己；
words.ex: The teacher enforced discipline in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 老师在教室里维持纪律。
words.en: Discipline is the practice of making people obey rules or standards of behaviour, and punishing them when they do not.

words.ex: He made a disclosure about the secret plan.
words.ex_cn: 他透露了这个秘密计划。
words.en: The act of making something known or the fact that is made known.

words.ex: They had a discord about the movie ending.
words.ex_cn: 他们对电影的结局有分歧。
words.en: Disagreement or strife between people or groups.

words.tr:
n. 折扣；
v. 不全信；不重视；
words.ex: The store gave a 20% discount on all shoes.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有鞋子提供了20%的折扣。
words.en: A reduction in the usual price of something, or the act of reducing the price.

words.ex: There is a discrepancy between the two reports.
words.ex_cn: 这两份报告之间有差异。
words.en: A discrepancy is a difference between two or more things that should be the same.

words.ex: The two groups are discrete and do not overlap.
words.ex_cn: 这两个群体是分离的，没有重叠。
words.en: Something that is discrete is separate and distinct in form or concept.

words.ex: The teacher gave students discretion to choose their own topic.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了学生自行选择题目的权利。
words.en: Discretion is the quality of behaving in a quiet and controlled way without drawing attention to yourself or giving away personal or private information.

words.tr: adj. 自由决定的；酌情行事的；便宜行事的
words.ex: He spent his discretionary money on a new phone.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的可自由支配的钱花在了一部新手机上。
words.en: If something is discretionary, it is available for use as someone chooses, rather than according to a set plan or rule.

words.ex: They discriminate against people because of their race.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为种族而歧视他人。
words.en: To discriminate means to recognize a distinction; differentiate. It can also mean to make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, sex, or age.

words.tr: adj. 鄙视的；不屑一顾的；轻蔑的
words.ex: He gave a disdainful look at the messy room.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看了一眼凌乱的房间。
words.en: If you are disdainful of someone or something, you dislike them because you think that they are inferior or unimportant.

words.tr: v. 剥夺…的权利（尤指选举权）
words.ex: The law disenfranchises many poor people.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律剥夺了许多穷人的投票权。
words.en: To disenfranchise someone means to take away their right to vote or to deprive them of a privilege or a right.

words.ex: They will dismantle the old bridge next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周将拆除这座旧桥。
words.en: To dismantle something means to take it to pieces.

words.ex: He felt dismay when he saw the low grade.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到低分时，感到沮丧。
words.en: Dismay is a feeling of unhappiness and disappointment.

words.ex: He dismissed her advice and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他不理会她的建议，走开了。
words.en: If you dismiss someone, you send them away or allow them to leave.

words.tr: v. 使迷失方向；使迷惘
words.ex: The storm disoriented the hikers.
words.ex_cn: 风暴使徒步者迷失了方向。
words.en: To cause someone to lose their sense of direction or to become confused.

words.tr:
adj. 蔑视的；毁谤的；轻视的
v. 轻视；蔑视；贬损；“disparage”的现在分词
words.ex: He made a disparaging comment about his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友说了句贬低的话。
words.en: If you are disparaging about someone or something, or make disparaging comments about them, you say things which criticize them and show that you do not have a good opinion of them.

words.ex: The two cultures are disparate in their traditions.
words.ex_cn: 这两种文化在传统上完全不同。
words.en: Things that are disparate are clearly different from each other in quality or type.

words.ex: He tried to dispel the fear with calm words.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用平静的话语消除恐惧。
words.en: To dispel something such as a fear, belief, or idea means to make it disappear or to make people stop believing it.

words.ex: The nurse will dispense medicine to the patients.
words.ex_cn: 护士将分发药品给病人。
words.en: To dispense means to distribute or provide something, especially in a systematic way, or to prepare and give out medicine.

words.ex: The police dispersed the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 警察驱散了人群。
words.en: If a crowd of people disperses or is dispersed, it breaks up and the people go in different directions.

words.tr: v. 取代；迫使…离开家园；
words.ex: The new robot will displace the workers on the assembly line.
words.ex_cn: 这个新机器人将取代装配线上的工人。
words.en: To displace something or someone means to take their place or to force them to leave their usual place or role.

words.ex: He disposed of the old books.
words.ex_cn: 他处理了那些旧书。
words.en: To dispose of something means to get rid of it, especially by throwing it away.

words.ex: The punishment was disproportionate to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 惩罚与罪行不成比例。
words.en: Something that is disproportionate is surprisingly large or small in comparison to something else.

words.tr:
n. 纠纷；争端；
v. 对（某事）有异议；
words.ex: The dispute between the two neighbors was about the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间的纠纷是关于篱笆的。
words.en: A dispute is a disagreement or argument about something important.

words.ex: The storm disrupted the train service.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴中断了火车服务。
words.en: To disrupt a system, process, or event means to prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way.

words.ex: The news will disseminate quickly through social media.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻会通过社交媒体迅速传播。
words.en: To disseminate means to spread or distribute something, especially information, widely.

words.ex: He expressed dissent about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定提出了异议。
words.en: Dissent is strong disagreement or dissatisfaction with a decision or opinion, especially one that is supported by most people or by people in authority.

words.tr: adj. 不相似的；不一样的；不同的
words.ex: The two apples are dissimilar in color.
words.ex_cn: 这两个苹果颜色不同。
words.en: If one thing is dissimilar to another, or if two things are dissimilar, they are very different from each other.

words.tr: v. 驱散；消散；浪费；挥霍
words.ex: The fog will dissipate by noon.
words.ex_cn: 雾将在中午前消散。
words.en: If something dissipates or is dissipated, it becomes less or becomes less strong until it disappears or goes away completely.

words.tr: v. 使分离；脱离；与…无关
words.ex: He tries to dissociate himself from the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 他试图让自己与坏消息脱离关系。
words.en: If you dissociate yourself from something or someone, you deliberately avoid being connected with them, especially because you want to avoid being affected by something bad or harmful.

words.tr: v. 蒸馏；用蒸馏法提取；蒸馏出；提炼
words.ex: They distill water to remove impurities.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过蒸馏去除水中的杂质。
words.en: To distill a liquid means to purify it by heating it until it becomes a gas and then cooling it so that it becomes a liquid again. This process can also be used to extract the essential elements or meanings from something.

words.ex: The two colors are distinct.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色有区别。
words.en: If something is distinct, it is easily seen, heard, or understood.

words.ex: This painting has a distinctive style.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有独特的风格。
words.en: Something that is distinctive has a special quality or feature which makes it easily recognizable and different from other things of the same type.

words.ex: The two colors distinguish the two teams.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色使两个队伍有所不同。
words.en: If you can distinguish one thing from another, you can see or understand how they are different.

words.ex: The mirror distorts my face.
words.ex_cn: 这面镜子扭曲了我的脸。
words.en: If you distort a statement, fact, or idea, you report or represent it in an untrue way.

words.ex: The teacher will distribute the books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将把书分发给学生。
words.en: If you distribute things, you hand them or deliver them to a number of people.

words.ex: The distribution of students in the class is even.
words.ex_cn: 班级里学生的分布是均匀的。
words.en: The process of giving out or spreading something, or the way in which something is spread or arranged over an area or among a group of people.

words.ex: The distributor delivers snacks to local stores.
words.ex_cn: 这家经销商将零食配送到本地商店。
words.en: A distributor is a company or person that supplies goods to shops or other businesses, or a device that sends out electricity to the spark plugs in an engine.

words.ex: This district has many parks and schools.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区有许多公园和学校。
words.en: A district is a part of a city, country, or other area that has been officially designated for a particular purpose, such as administration or business.

words.ex: Please don't disturb me while I'm reading.
words.ex_cn: 我读书时请不要打扰我。
words.en: To disturb someone means to interrupt what they are doing and cause them inconvenience or annoyance.

words.ex: The two roads diverge after the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 两条路在桥后分岔。
words.en: If one thing diverges from another similar thing, the first thing becomes different from the second or develops differently from it. You can also say that two things diverge.

words.tr: adj. 不同的；多种多样的；
words.ex: The class has diverse students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级有来自许多国家的不同学生。
words.en: If a group or range of things is diverse, it is made up of a wide variety of things.

words.ex: The company wants diversification to reduce risk.
words.ex_cn: 公司希望通过多元化来降低风险。
words.en: Diversification is the act of making something more diverse or varied, especially in business contexts where it refers to expanding into new markets or products.

words.ex: The company plans to diversify its products.
words.ex_cn: 公司计划使产品多样化。
words.en: To diversify means to make or become more varied or different. It often refers to the process of a company or individual expanding their range of products or activities to reduce risk or to explore new opportunities.

words.ex: The loud music was a diversion from his worries.
words.ex_cn: 那嘈杂的音乐分散了他对烦恼的注意力。
words.en: A diversion is an action or event that attracts your attention away from what you are doing or should be doing.

words.ex: The government decided to divest the company of its assets.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定剥夺该公司的资产。
words.en: If you divest someone of power, rights, or authority, you take those things away from them. If you divest yourself of something that you own or are responsible for, you get rid of it or stop being responsible for it.

words.tr: n. 被除数；股份红利；股息
words.ex: In 12 ÷ 3 = 4, the dividend is 12.
words.en: A dividend is a sum of money paid regularly (typically annually) by a company to its shareholders out of its profits (or reserves).

words.tr: adj. 可被整除的；可分的
words.ex: The number 12 is divisible by 3.
words.ex_cn: 12 能被 3 整除。
words.en: Capable of being divided, especially with no remainder.

words.ex: The division of the cake was fair.
words.ex_cn: 蛋糕的划分是公平的。
words.en: The act or process of dividing something into parts or the state of being divided.

words.ex: The divisive comment caused a fight among friends.
words.ex_cn: 这个制造分裂的言论引发了朋友们之间的争吵。
words.en: Causing or likely to cause disagreement or division between people.

words.ex: He won't divulge the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他不会泄露这个秘密。
words.en: If you divulge a piece of secret or private information, you tell it to someone.

words.ex: He earned his doctorate in biology.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了生物学博士学位。
words.en: A doctorate is the highest level of academic degree awarded by universities, following the completion of a course of study demonstrating the ability to conduct independent research.

words.ex: The church teaches its doctrine to all members.
words.ex_cn: 教会向所有成员传授它的教义。
words.en: A doctrine is a set of beliefs or principles that are taught or accepted by a particular group, especially in religion or politics.

words.ex: He submitted the documentation for his project.
words.ex_cn: 他提交了项目的文件。
words.en: Documentation refers to the act of providing documents or the documents themselves, which serve as evidence or records of something.

words.ex: He refuses to accept the dogma of the church.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝接受教会的教条。
words.en: A principle or set of principles laid down by an authority as incontrovertibly true.

words.ex: He is an expert in the domain of artificial intelligence.
words.ex_cn: 他是人工智能领域的专家。
words.en: A domain is a particular field of thought, activity, or interest, especially one over which someone has control, influence, or rights.

words.tr: adj. 家庭的；国内的；驯养的；
words.ex: She prefers domestic chores over going out.
words.ex_cn: 她更喜欢做家务而不是外出。
words.en: Domestic means relating to the home, family, or household affairs. It can also refer to something that is made or produced within a country and not imported.

words.ex: Humans domesticated dogs thousands of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 人类几千年前就驯养了狗。
words.en: To domesticate an animal or plant means to bring it under human control in order to provide food, power, or company.

words.ex: The domestication of dogs began thousands of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 狗的驯养始于数千年前。
words.en: The process of taming an animal and keeping it as a pet or on a farm, or the cultivation of a plant for food.

words.ex: She missed the quiet domesticity of her childhood home.
words.ex_cn: 她怀念童年家园的宁静家庭生活。
words.en: Domesticity refers to home or family life, especially the activities and duties involved in running a household.

words.ex: He dominates the conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他主宰了谈话。
words.en: To dominate means to control or govern someone or something, or to be the most important or noticeable feature of something.

words.ex: He donate money to the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他向贫困儿童捐赠钱。
words.en: To donate means to give something, especially money, to a person or organization that needs help.

words.tr: adj. 休眠的；蛰伏的；暂停活动的
words.ex: The volcano is dormant now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Something that is dormant is not active or growing but has the ability to be active at a later time.

words.ex: The doctor adjusted the dosage of the medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生调整了药物的剂量。
words.en: The amount of a medicine or drug that is taken at one time or over a period of time.

words.ex: The doctor gave him a small dose of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他一小剂量的药。
words.en: A dose of a medicine or a drug is the amount of it that you take at one time, or the amount that is recommended for you to take.

words.ex: He kneaded the dough for bread.
words.ex_cn: 他揉了做面包的生面团。
words.en: Dough is a thick, malleable mixture of flour and liquid, used for baking into bread or pastry. It can also informally refer to money.

words.ex: He tries to downplay his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他试图淡化自己的错误。
words.en: To downplay something means to make it seem less important or less bad than it really is.

words.tr:
adv. 朝下游方向；
adj. 下游的；
words.ex: The boat moved downstream with the current.
words.ex_cn: 船顺流而下。
words.en: In the direction in which a stream or river flows; situated or moving in the direction of the flow of a stream or river.

words.ex: The walls were painted a drab color.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁被刷成了土褐色。
words.en: If you describe something as drab, you think that it is dull and boring to look at or experience.

words.ex: He wrote a draft of the letter before sending it.
words.ex_cn: 他在发送之前写了这封信的草稿。
words.en: A draft is a preliminary version of a piece of writing, or a current of air in a room or other confined space. It can also refer to the act of selecting someone for a particular purpose or task, especially in sports or the military.

words.ex: The city improved its drainage system after the flood.
words.ex_cn: 洪水之后，这座城市改进了它的排水系统。
words.en: Drainage is the system or process by which water or other liquids are drained from a place.

words.tr: v. 改编为戏剧；渲染；使戏剧化
words.ex: They dramatize the novel for the stage.
words.ex_cn: 他们将这部小说改编成舞台剧。
words.en: If a book or story is dramatized, it is written or presented as a play, film, or television drama.

words.ex: The company made drastic cuts to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司进行了急剧的削减以节省资金。
words.en: If you describe a change or action as drastic, you mean that it is extreme and often severe.

words.tr:
n. 流动；
v. 漂移；
words.ex: The drift of the river carries leaves downstream.
words.ex_cn: 河流的流动将树叶冲向下游。
words.en: If something or someone drifts somewhere, they move there slowly or gradually. As a noun, drift can refer to a slow, gradual movement or change, or the general meaning or intent of something.

words.tr: n. 钻探；操练； v. 钻孔；“drill”的现在分词；
words.ex: The company started drilling for oil last month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司上个月开始钻探石油。
words.en: The act of making holes in something using a drill, or the process of training people to perform a task or to behave in a certain way.

words.tr:
v. 下毛毛雨；（毛毛雨似的）洒落
n. 毛毛细雨
words.ex: It is drizzling outside.
words.ex_cn: 外面正在下毛毛雨。
words.en: Light rain falling in very fine drops.

words.ex: A droplet fell from the leaf.
words.ex_cn: 一滴水从叶子上落下。
words.en: A droplet is a very small drop of a liquid.

words.ex: He became a dropout after failing math class.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试不及格后退学了。
words.en: A dropout is a person who leaves school or college before they have finished their studies, especially because they are not interested in continuing.

words.ex: The drought made it hard to grow crops.
words.ex_cn: 旱灾使种植庄稼变得困难。
words.en: A drought is a long period of time during which no rain falls and hence there is a shortage of water.

words.tr: adj. 可疑的；怀疑的；拿不准的；
words.ex: The deal seemed dubious to me.
words.ex_cn: 这个交易在我看来很可疑。
words.en: If you describe something as dubious, you mean that you do not consider it to be completely honest, safe, or reliable.

words.tr: adj. 可延展的；易于塑造的
words.ex: The gold is ductile and can be drawn into thin wires.
words.ex_cn: 金具有延展性，可以拉成细丝。
words.en: A ductile material is one that can be stretched into a wire or hammered into a thin sheet without breaking.

words.ex: He dumped the trash into the bin.
words.ex_cn: 他把垃圾倒进了垃圾桶。
words.en: To dump something means to get rid of it quickly and without care, often because it is no longer wanted or needed. It can also refer to the place where waste is left.

words.tr: n. 垃圾箱；垃圾罐；大垃圾箱
words.ex: He threw the trash into the dumpster.
words.ex_cn: 他把垃圾扔进了垃圾箱。
words.en: A dumpster is a large metal container for waste, designed to be emptied into a garbage truck.

words.tr: v. 复制；复印；再做一次；
words.ex: He duplicated the file to save a copy.
words.ex_cn: 他复制了该文件以保存一份副本。
words.en: To duplicate something means to make an exact copy of it.

words.ex: The duplication of the document cost five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 这份文件的复制花了五美元。
words.en: the act or process of making an exact copy of something

words.ex: The durability of this plastic makes it good for outdoor use.
words.ex_cn: 这种塑料的持久性使它适合户外使用。
words.en: The ability of something to last a long time without significant deterioration.

words.ex: The duration of the movie is two hours.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的持续时间是两小时。
words.en: The duration of an event or state is the time during which it happens or exists.

words.ex: The fairy tale features a dwarf who lives in a small house.
words.ex_cn: 这个童话故事中有一个住在小房子里的侏儒。
words.en: A dwarf is a person, animal, or plant that is much smaller than the usual size of its species. As a verb, to dwarf means to make someone or something seem small or insignificant in comparison.

words.tr:
n. 住宅；住所
v. 居住；栖身；沉湎于；“dwell”的现在分词
words.ex: He lives in a small dwelling near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边的一个小住所里。
words.en: A dwelling is a place where someone lives, such as a house or apartment.

words.ex: The water in the pond dwindles in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天时，池塘里的水逐渐减少。
words.en: If something dwindles, it becomes smaller, weaker, or less in number.

words.tr:
n. 染料；
v. 给...染色；
words.ex: She bought a natural dye to color her fabric.
words.ex_cn: 她买了一种天然染料来给布料染色。
words.en: A dye is a substance used to change the color of something permanently. To dye something means to change its color by applying a dye.

words.tr:
adj. 动态的；有活力的；不断变化的；
n. 活力；动力；
words.ex: The game has dynamic weather that changes every hour.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏有每小时变化的动态天气。
words.en: If you describe someone as dynamic, you approve of them because they are full of energy or full of new ideas.

words.tr:
n. 安逸；轻松；
v. 缓解；减轻；
words.ex: He enjoys the ease of living in a quiet village.
words.ex_cn: 他享受住在安静村庄里的安逸。
words.en: If you talk about the ease of a particular activity, you are referring to the way that it has been made easier to do, or to the fact that it is already easy to do. Ease is also a state of being comfortable and without worry or anxiety.

words.ex: Bats use echolocation to find insects in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 蝙蝠利用回声定位在黑暗中寻找昆虫。
words.en: Echolocation is a method used by certain animals to determine the location of objects by emitting sound waves and listening for the echo.

words.tr:
n. 日食；月食；黯然失色
v. 使失色
words.ex: We watched the solar eclipse last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚观看了日食。
words.en: An eclipse occurs when one celestial body moves into the shadow of another, temporarily obscuring it or cutting off its light.

words.ex: He studies ecology to understand how animals live with plants.
words.ex_cn: 他学习生态学以了解动物如何与植物共存。
words.en: Ecology is the study of the relationships between living organisms, including humans, and their physical environment; it seeks to understand the vital connections between plants and animals and the world around them.

words.ex: The country's economy is growing fast.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家的经济正在快速增长。
words.en: The economy of a country or region is the system by which money, industry, and trade are organized.

words.ex: The forest is a healthy ecosystem.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林是一个健康的生态系统。
words.en: An ecosystem is a complex network or interconnected system, especially one that involves a community of living organisms in conjunction with their environment.

words.ex: The edge of the table is sharp.
words.ex_cn: 桌子的边缘很锋利。
words.en: The edge of something is the place or line where it stops, or the part of it that is furthest from the middle.

words.tr: adj. 可食用的；可以吃的；
words.ex: These mushrooms are edible and safe to eat.
words.ex_cn: 这些蘑菇是可食用的，安全可以吃。
words.en: Fit to be eaten as food.

words.tr:
n. 社论；
adj. 编辑的；
words.ex: The newspaper published an editorial about climate change.
words.ex_cn: 报纸发表了一篇关于气候变化的社论。
words.en: An editorial is an article in a newspaper which gives the opinion of the editor or publisher on a topic or item of news.

words.ex: The educator helps students learn math.
words.ex_cn: 这位教育者帮助学生学习数学。
words.en: An educator is a person who educates people, especially as a job.

words.tr: n. 影响；作用；效果；效应；
words.ex: The new law had a big effect on traffic.
words.ex_cn: 新法律对交通产生了很大影响。
words.en: A change that is a result or consequence of an action or other cause.

words.ex: The efficacy of the medicine is clear.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物的效果是明显的。
words.en: The ability to produce a desired or intended result.

words.ex: The new machine improves the efficiency of production.
words.ex_cn: 这台新机器提高了生产的效率。
words.en: Efficiency is the ability to do something or produce something without wasting materials, time, or energy.

words.ex: He uses an efficient way to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种高效的方法解决数学问题。
words.en: If something or someone is efficient, they are able to do tasks successfully, without wasting time or energy.

words.tr: n. （名人）雕像；（丑化的）模拟像
words.ex: They burned an effigy of the king.
words.ex_cn: 他们烧了一个国王的雕像。
words.en: An effigy is a sculpture or model of a person, often made to be destroyed as a protest or as part of a ceremony.

words.tr: n. 废水；污物；水流 adj. 流出的
words.ex: The factory releases effluent into the river.
words.ex_cn: 工厂将废水排入河中。
words.en: Effluent is liquid waste material that comes out of factories or sewage works.

words.tr: n. 平等主义；平均主义；
words.ex: He believes in egalitarianism and treats everyone equally.
words.ex_cn: 他相信平等主义，并平等地对待每个人。
words.en: Egalitarianism is the belief in or practice of equality among all people, especially in political, economic, or social spheres.

words.tr: adj. 自我中心的；自私自利的
words.ex: He is egoistic and only thinks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他很自私，只考虑自己。
words.en: Egoistic refers to someone who is excessively self-centered or self-interested.

words.ex: He reject the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这份工作邀请。
words.en: If you reject something such as a proposal, a request, or an offer, you do not accept it or you do not agree to it.

words.tr:
adj. 精心制作的；详尽的；
v. 精心制作；详尽阐述；
words.ex: She wore an elaborate dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件精心制作的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: To elaborate means to add more details to something that has already been said or written, making it more complex or detailed. As an adjective, it describes something that is very complex and detailed.

words.tr:
adj. 选举的；选修的；可选择的
n. 选修课程
words.ex: He voted in the elective process for mayor.
words.ex_cn: 他参加了市长的选举过程。
words.en: An elective course or subject is one that you can choose to study as part of your course, rather than one that you have to study.

words.ex: The electorate voted for a new leader.
words.ex_cn: 选民投票选出了新领导人。
words.en: The electorate refers to all the people in a country or area who are entitled to vote in an election.

words.ex: The town lost electricity during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴期间，这个城镇停电了。
words.en: A form of energy resulting from the existence of charged particles (such as electrons or protons), either statically as an accumulation of charge or dynamically as a current.

words.tr: n. 电镀物品; vt. 电镀
words.ex: The electro fan stopped working.
words.ex_cn: 这个电风扇不工作了。
words.en: Electro is a prefix or combining form indicating electricity or electronic.

words.ex: The electromagnetic wave travels through space.
words.ex_cn: 电磁波在太空中传播。
words.en: Relating to the interrelation of electric currents or fields and magnetic fields.

words.ex: The electron moves around the nucleus.
words.ex_cn: 电子围绕原子核运动。
words.en: An electron is a tiny particle with a negative charge that is found in all atoms and plays a key role in electricity.

words.ex: Water is made of two elements: hydrogen and oxygen.
words.ex_cn: 水由两种要素组成：氢和氧。
words.en: An element is a substance that cannot be separated into simpler substances by chemical means and is composed of atoms having the same number of protons.

words.ex: Exercise can elevate your mood.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提升你的情绪。
words.en: To elevate something means to raise it to a higher position or level, either physically or in terms of its status or importance.

words.ex: The elevation of his skills helped him get a better job.
words.ex_cn: 他技能的提升帮助他找到了一份更好的工作。
words.en: The height to which something is elevated or to which it rises.

words.ex: The teacher asked a simple question to elicit answers from students.
words.ex_cn: 老师问了一个简单的问题来引出学生的回答。
words.en: To elicit a response or a reaction means to cause it to happen by something that you say or do.

words.tr: adj. 有资格的；合格的；合意的；
words.ex: He is eligible to vote because he is 18 years old.
words.ex_cn: 他年满18岁，有资格投票。
words.en: Someone who is eligible for something is qualified or allowed to do it.

words.ex: We must eliminate the waste to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须消除浪费以保护环境。
words.en: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.

words.ex: The elite of the city often meet at private clubs.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的精英经常在私人俱乐部会面。
words.en: You can refer to the most powerful, rich, or talented people within a particular group, place, or society as the elite.

words.ex: The track is elliptical in shape.
words.ex_cn: 这个跑道是椭圆形的。
words.en: Something that is elliptical has the shape of an ellipse or is characterized by the omission of words that are understood to be obvious.

words.ex: The artist elongated the figure to create a sense of grace.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家拉长了人物形象，以创造出一种优雅的感觉。
words.en: To elongate something means to make it longer, especially by stretching it.

words.tr: adj. 雄辩的；有口才的；有说服力的
words.ex: He gave an eloquent speech at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上发表了富有感染力的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as eloquent, you mean that they are able to express their ideas and opinions well, so that other people understand them and are influenced by them.

words.ex: The tricky question eluded even the best students.
words.ex_cn: 这道难题难倒了即使是最优秀的学生。
words.en: If something that you want eludes you, you fail to obtain it. If you elude someone or something, you avoid them or escape from them.

words.ex: The emancipation of slaves ended centuries of oppression.
words.ex_cn: 奴隶的解放结束了几个世纪的压迫。
words.en: The act of freeing someone from legal, social, or political restrictions.

words.tr: vt. 铭记于心；使不朽；防腐；使充满香气
words.ex: They embalm the memory of their hero.
words.ex_cn: 他们铭记着英雄的记忆。
words.en: To embalm a dead body means to treat it with special substances to prevent it from decaying.

words.tr:
n. 禁止贸易令；禁运
v. 禁止…的贸易；禁运
words.ex: The country placed an embargo on imported goods.
words.ex_cn: 该国对进口商品实施了禁运。
words.en: An embargo is an official order to stop trade with another country.

words.ex: He decided to embark on a new career.
words.ex_cn: 他决定从事一份新职业。
words.en: To embark on something means to start it, especially something new, difficult, or exciting.

words.ex: He embarrassed himself in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班同学面前让自己丢脸了。
words.en: If you embarrass someone, you make them feel shy, ashamed, or guilty about something.

words.tr: adj. 尴尬的；窘迫的； v. “embarrass”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He felt embarrassed when he tripped in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在大家面前绊倒时感到很尴尬。
words.en: If you are embarrassed, you feel shy or ashamed because of something that you have done or that has happened to you.

words.ex: He embeds the photo in the document.
words.ex_cn: 他把照片插入到文档中。
words.en: To fix something firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass.

words.ex: She embellished the dress with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她用花朵装饰了这条裙子。
words.en: To embellish something means to make it more attractive by adding decorative details or features.

words.ex: He finally embraced the new idea.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了这个新想法。
words.en: To take someone into your arms as a sign of love or affection, or to accept something enthusiastically.

words.ex: The embryo grows inside the mother's womb.
words.ex_cn: 胚胎在母亲的子宫内生长。
words.en: An embryo is an unborn animal or human being in the very early stages of development.

words.ex: The embryonic stage is the earliest phase of development.
words.ex_cn: 胚胎阶段是发育的最早时期。
words.en: In an early stage of development; rudimentary.

words.ex: A bird emerged from the trees.
words.ex_cn: 一只鸟从树中浮现出来。
words.en: If something or someone emerges, they come out of or move out of something and become visible.

words.ex: The emergence of new technology changed our lives.
words.ex_cn: 新技术的出现改变了我们的生活。
words.en: The process of coming into view or becoming exposed after being concealed.

words.ex: He called an emergency doctor when he felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 当他感到不舒服时，他叫了急诊医生。
words.en: An emergency is an unexpected and usually dangerous situation that calls for immediate action.

words.ex: He wants to emigrate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他想移民到加拿大过更好的生活。
words.en: To leave one's own country in order to settle permanently in another.

words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.ex: The factory reduces emission to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 工厂减少排放以保护环境。
words.en: An emission is the production and discharge of something, especially gas or radiation.

words.ex: The lamp emits a soft light.
words.ex_cn: 灯发出柔和的光。
words.en: To emit means to send out something such as light, heat, sound, gas, etc.

words.ex: The teacher put emphasis on reading every day.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调每天都要阅读。
words.en: Special importance, value, or prominence given to something.

words.ex: He emphasizes the importance of homework.
words.ex_cn: 他强调作业的重要性。
words.en: To give special importance or prominence to (something) in speaking or writing.

words.tr: adj. 经验主义的；以经验为根据的；
words.ex: The scientist used empirical data to support her theory.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家使用经验数据来支持她的理论。
words.en: Empirical evidence or study relies on practical experience rather than theories.

words.ex: He works hard to emulate his older brother.
words.ex_cn: 他努力赶上他的哥哥。
words.en: To emulate someone or something means to try to be like them or to do something in the same way that they do it.

words.tr: v. 制定（法律）；通过（法律）；扮演（角色）
words.ex: The government will enact a new law next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将颁布一项新法律。
words.en: To enact a law or rule means to make it official by passing it through a legislative body.

words.ex: He brushed his teeth to protect the enamel.
words.ex_cn: 他刷牙以保护牙釉质。
words.en: A hard, glossy substance that is applied to metal, glass, or pottery for decoration or protection.

words.ex: Encephalitis is a serious condition that requires immediate medical attention.
words.ex_cn: 脑炎是一种需要立即就医的严重疾病。
words.en: Encephalitis is an inflammation of the brain, usually caused by a viral infection.

words.ex: They enclose the garden with a wooden fence.
words.ex_cn: 他们用木栅栏把花园围起来。
words.en: If you enclose something with a letter, you put it in the same envelope as the letter.

words.ex: He will encode the message with a secret code.
words.ex_cn: 他将用密钥对这条信息进行编码。
words.en: To convert information into a particular form, especially for the purposes of secrecy or transmission.

words.ex: The book encompasses all basic math skills.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了所有基础数学技能。
words.en: If something encompasses particular things, it includes them.

words.tr:
v. 遭遇；遇到；邂逅；
n. 遭遇；
words.ex: He encountered a bear while hiking in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他在森林里徒步时遭遇了一只熊。
words.en: If you encounter problems or difficulties, you experience them.

words.tr: v. 侵入；侵占；侵犯；侵蚀
words.ex: The new building encroaches on the park.
words.ex_cn: 新建筑侵占了公园。
words.en: To gradually take something such as power or authority from someone else, often in a way that is not fair or legal.

words.ex: He looked up the word in an encyclopedia.
words.ex_cn: 他从百科全书中查找这个词。
words.en: An encyclopedia is a book or set of books giving information on many subjects or on many aspects of one subject and typically arranged alphabetically.

words.tr: v. 使遭危险或伤害；危害；危及
words.ex: Pollution can endanger animals.
words.ex_cn: 污染会危及动物。
words.en: To put someone or something at risk or in danger.

words.tr:
n. 尽力；尝试；
v. 尽力；奋力；
words.ex: His endeavor to finish the project took all his energy.
words.ex_cn: 他为完成这个项目付出了全部努力。
words.en: An endeavor is an attempt to do something, especially something new or original.

words.ex: Malaria is endemic in some parts of Africa.
words.ex_cn: 疟疾在非洲某些地区是地方性的。
words.en: If a disease or condition is endemic in a particular area, it is frequently or regularly found among the people living there.

words.ex: Running releases endorphin and makes you happy.
words.ex_cn: 跑步会释放内啡肽，让你感到快乐。
words.en: Endorphins are chemicals produced naturally by the nervous system to cope with pain or stress. They are often called 'feel-good' chemicals because they can act as pain relievers and happiness boosters.

words.ex: The coach endorses the new player.
words.ex_cn: 教练支持这位新球员。
words.en: If you endorse someone or something, you say publicly that you support or approve of them.

words.ex: The reaction is endothermic and needs heat.
words.ex_cn: 这个反应是吸热的，需要热量。
words.en: (of a chemical reaction or compound) occurring or formed with absorption of heat

words.ex: The police enforce the law.
words.ex_cn: 警察强制执行法律。
words.en: If people in authority enforce a law or a rule, they make sure that it is obeyed, usually by punishing people who do not obey it.

words.tr: n. 解放；选举权的授予
words.ex: The enfranchisement of women gave them the right to vote.
words.ex_cn: 妇女的解放赋予了她们投票权。
words.en: Enfranchisement refers to the granting of the right to vote or the act of freeing someone from legal, social, or political restrictions.

words.tr: v. 参与；从事；吸引；与…建立密切关系；
words.ex: He engages in community volunteer work.
words.ex_cn: 他参与社区志愿工作。
words.en: To engage means to occupy, attract, or involve someone or oneself in a particular activity or situation.

words.ex: Poverty can engender crime.
words.ex_cn: 贫困会引起犯罪。
words.en: To cause a feeling, situation, or condition to exist.

words.ex: The fire engulfed the old house.
words.ex_cn: 大火吞噬了那座老房子。
words.en: If one thing engulfs another, it completely covers or hides it, often in a sudden and unexpected way.

words.ex: Exercise can enhance your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提高你的健康。
words.en: To enhance something means to improve its value, quality, or attractiveness.

words.tr: v. 增强；提高；“enhance”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 增强的；提高的；
words.ex: The new software enhanced the camera's quality.
words.ex_cn: 新软件增强了相机的画质。
words.en: If something is enhanced, it is made better or more effective.

words.tr:
adj. 开明的；有见识的；启迪的
v. 启发；开导；“enlighten”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is an enlightened teacher who helps students think clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位开明的老师，帮助学生清晰思考。
words.en: If you describe someone or their attitudes as enlightened, you mean that they have sensible, modern attitudes and ways of dealing with things.

words.tr: v. 参军；入伍；谋求（某人的帮助）
words.ex: He wants to enlist in the army.
words.ex_cn: 他想参军。
words.en: To enlist means to join the military, or to get someone else to join the military. It can also mean to get support or help from someone for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The elephant is enormous.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象非常巨大。
words.en: If you describe something as enormous, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size or amount.

words.ex: The new job enriched his life.
words.ex_cn: 这份新工作使他的生活富裕起来。
words.en: To enrich something means to improve its quality, often by adding something to it.

words.ex: He will enroll in the English course next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周将注册英语课程。
words.en: To officially register or enlist oneself or someone else in a course, institution, or organization.

words.tr: n. 全体；剧团；合奏曲；套装
words.ex: The ensemble played a beautiful song at the concert.
words.ex_cn: 这个合奏团在音乐会上演奏了一首优美的曲子。
words.en: An ensemble is a group of musicians, actors, or dancers who perform together.

words.tr: v. 置入神龛中；入庙祀奉；奉为神圣；珍藏
words.ex: They enshrined the ancient statue in a golden shrine.
words.ex_cn: 他们把这尊古代雕像置入了一个金色神龛中。
words.en: If something such as a tradition or a right is enshrined in something such as a constitution or law, it is protected by it.

words.ex: Running a business entails hard work.
words.ex_cn: 经营企业必然需要努力工作。
words.en: If one thing entails another, it involves it or causes it.

words.ex: This small enterprise makes handmade toys.
words.ex_cn: 这家小企业生产手工玩具。
words.en: An enterprise is a company or business, often a large one, or a difficult or important project, especially one that involves a lot of planning and organization.

words.ex: Watching movies is a popular entertainment.
words.ex_cn: 看电影是一种流行的休闲娱乐。
words.en: Entertainment refers to performances or activities that are intended to amuse or interest an audience.

words.ex: She cheered enthusiastically for her team.
words.ex_cn: 她热情地为她的队伍加油。
words.en: If you do something enthusiastically, you do it with great eagerness and excitement.

words.ex: The shop tries to entice customers with cheap prices.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店试图以低价吸引顾客。
words.en: If you entice someone, you attract them to a particular place or activity by making it seem attractive or interesting.

words.tr: v. 授权；命名；给...权利（或资格）
words.ex: This book entitles you to a free gift.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使你有资格获得一份免费礼物。
words.en: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

words.ex: The company is a legal entity.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是一个法律实体。
words.en: An entity is something that exists separately from other things and has a clear identity of its own.

words.tr: n. 进入者；新到者；新成员
words.ex: The entrant must pass the test to join.
words.ex_cn: 参赛者必须通过考试才能加入。
words.en: An entrant is someone who joins a particular group, organization, or activity, especially in order to take part in a competition or an examination.

words.ex: The defense argued that the evidence was obtained through entrapment.
words.ex_cn: 辩护方认为证据是通过诱捕手段获得的。
words.en: Entrapment is the act of tricking someone into committing a crime so that they can be arrested for it.

words.tr: n. 企业家；创业者；承包人；
words.ex: He is an entrepreneur who started a small coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位创办了小型咖啡店的企业家。
words.en: An entrepreneur is a person who organizes and operates a business or businesses, taking on greater than normal financial risks in order to do so.

words.ex: His entrepreneurship helped start a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他的企业家精神帮助创办了一家小企业。
words.en: Entrepreneurship is the activity of setting up a business or businesses, taking on financial risks in the hope of profit.

words.tr: n. 进入；入口；条目；参与；参赛作品；
words.ex: The entry to the building is locked after 10 PM.
words.ex_cn: 建筑物在晚上10点后进入通道会被锁上。
words.en: An entry is the act of going into a place or the right to go into it. It can also refer to a door, gate, or passage by which you enter a place. Additionally, an entry can be a piece of information recorded in a book, list, or computer, or the act of recording it.

words.ex: He will enumerate the steps clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地列出这些步骤。
words.en: To enumerate means to mention things one by one.

words.ex: He put the letter in an envelope.
words.ex_cn: 他把信装进了一个信封。
words.en: An envelope is a flat, usually rectangular or square, paper container for a letter, which you seal before you send it by post.

words.ex: He envisions a world without war.
words.ex_cn: 他想象一个没有战争的世界。
words.en: To envision something is to imagine it as a future possibility; it is often used to describe the act of foreseeing or planning for the future.

words.ex: The enzyme helps break down food in the stomach.
words.ex_cn: 这种酶帮助分解胃里的食物。
words.en: An enzyme is a protein that acts as a catalyst to bring about a specific biochemical reaction.

words.tr: adj. 史诗的；叙事诗的；宏丽的；
words.ex: The movie tells an epic story of heroes and dragons.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影讲述了一个关于英雄和龙的史诗故事。
words.en: An epic is a long book, poem, or film, whose story extends over a long period of time or tells of great events.

words.ex: The earthquake started at the epicenter near the city.
words.ex_cn: 地震从城市附近的震中开始。
words.en: The point on the Earth's surface directly above the focus of an earthquake.

words.ex: The epidemic spread quickly across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这种流行病迅速蔓延到全国。
words.en: An epidemic is a large number of cases of an infectious disease occurring at the same time.

words.tr: n. 事件；一集；一段经历；
words.ex: The accident was a sad episode in his life.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是他生命中的一件悲伤的事。
words.en: An episode is a part of a story that is broadcast on television or radio as one of a series, or a single event or group of related events.

words.tr: adj. 插曲般的；由松散片段组成的；不定期发生的；
words.ex: The movie has an episodic structure, with each scene telling a small story.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影具有插曲般的结构，每个场景讲述一个小故事。
words.en: An episodic piece of writing or film consists of a series of separate events or episodes that are linked together.

words.tr: adj. 新纪元的；划时代的
words.ex: The invention of the internet was an epochal event.
words.ex_cn: 互联网的发明是一个划时代的事件。
words.en: An epochal event or change is one that is very important and has a great effect on future events.

words.tr: v. 使平等；使均等；使相等
words.ex: The law aims to equalize opportunities for all people.
words.ex_cn: 法律旨在使所有人机会平等。
words.en: To make things equal in amount, size, or value.

words.ex: The two kids stayed in equilibrium on the seesaw.
words.ex_cn: 两个孩子在跷跷板上保持了平衡。
words.en: A state in which opposing forces or influences are balanced.

words.ex: The school will equip the lab with new computers.
words.ex_cn: 学校将为实验室配备新电脑。
words.en: To provide someone or something with the necessary items for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He bought equity in a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了一家科技公司的股票。
words.en: Equity is the quality of being fair and impartial.

words.tr:
n. 等价物；
adj. 相等的；等价的；
words.ex: The dollar is the equivalent of ten yuan.
words.ex_cn: 美元是十元的等价物。
words.en: If one amount or value is the equivalent of another, they are the same.

words.ex: The invention of the internet changed our era.
words.ex_cn: 互联网的发明改变了我们的时代。
words.en: An era is a period of time that is considered as a single unit because of a particular characteristic or event.

words.ex: The government wants to eradicate poverty.
words.ex_cn: 政府希望消灭贫困。
words.en: To eradicate something means to get rid of it completely.

words.tr: n. 根除；连根拔除；消灭；
words.ex: The government aims at the eradication of poverty.
words.ex_cn: 政府的目标是根除贫困。
words.en: The complete destruction of something so that it no longer exists.

words.ex: He erased the wrong answer with an eraser.
words.ex_cn: 他用橡皮擦掉了错误的答案。
words.en: To erase something means to remove it completely from a surface or from a place where it is stored.

words.tr: adj. 人类环境改造学的；人类工程学的
words.ex: The chair is ergonomic and helps reduce back pain.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子符合人体工程学，有助于减轻背部疼痛。
words.en: Ergonomic refers to the study of people's efficiency in their working environment, especially the design of furniture and equipment to maximize comfort and efficiency.

words.tr: v. 侵蚀；腐蚀；逐渐丧失；削弱
words.ex: The wind erodes the sand slowly.
words.ex_cn: 风慢慢侵蚀着沙子。
words.en: If rock or soil erodes or is eroded by the weather, sea, or wind, it cracks and breaks so that it is gradually destroyed.

words.ex: He went on an errand to buy milk.
words.ex_cn: 他去买牛奶了。
words.en: An errand is a short journey that you make in order to do a job for someone, for example when you go to a shop to buy something for them.

words.tr: adj. 不稳定的；飘忽不定的；
words.ex: The weather has been erratic this month.
words.ex_cn: 这个月的天气一直不稳定。
words.en: Something that is erratic does not follow a regular pattern, but happens at unexpected times or moves in unexpected directions.

words.ex: The volcano had a big eruption last week.
words.ex_cn: 上周这座火山发生了大喷发。
words.en: An eruption is a sudden, often violent, outburst or discharge, such as that of a volcano, emotion, or conflict.

words.ex: The argument started small but soon escalate.
words.ex_cn: 争论起初很小，但很快逐步升高。
words.en: If a bad situation escalates or if someone or something escalates it, it becomes greater in size, seriousness, or intensity.

words.ex: He tries to eschew sugar for health reasons.
words.ex_cn: 他为了健康尽量避免吃糖。
words.en: If you eschew something, you deliberately avoid doing it or becoming involved in it.

words.ex: The essence of love is caring for others.
words.ex_cn: 爱的本质是关心他人。
words.en: The essence of something is its basic and most important characteristic which gives it its individual identity.

words.ex: The old estate has large gardens and a beautiful mansion.
words.ex_cn: 这个古老的庄园有大片花园和一座美丽的豪宅。
words.en: An estate is all the money and property that someone owns, especially everything that is left when they die.

words.ex: He earned the esteem of his colleagues through hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作赢得了同事们的尊重。
words.en: If you esteem someone or something, you respect or admire them.

words.tr:
v. 估算；估价；
n. 估价；估算；
words.ex: Can you estimate how long it will take?
words.ex_cn: 你能估算一下需要多长时间吗？
words.en: If you estimate a quantity or value, you make an approximate judgment or calculation of it.

words.tr: phrase. 以及其他人；等人；“et alibi”的缩写
words.ex: The study was conducted by Dr. Smith et al.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究是由史密斯博士等人进行的。
words.en: An abbreviation for 'et alii' (and others), used in citations to indicate that there are additional authors.

words.tr: v.取来; 接来; 到达; 吸引（fetch 的过去分词形式）; 拿; 取物; 卖得（fetch 的过去...
words.ex: He fetched water from the well.
words.ex_cn: 他从井里打水。
words.en: To go and bring back something or someone.

words.ex: The stars seem eternal in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中的星星看起来是永久的。
words.en: If something is eternal, it lasts forever.

words.ex: Ethanol is used as a fuel in some cars.
words.ex_cn: 乙醇被用作一些汽车的燃料。
words.en: Ethanol is a clear, colorless liquid that is used as a solvent, in the manufacture of other chemicals, and as a fuel additive.

words.tr: n. 道德规范；伦理标准；
words.ex: The company follows a strong ethic of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司遵循诚实的道德规范。
words.en: An ethic is a moral principle or set of moral principles that guides the behavior of a person or group, especially in a professional context.

words.ex: The festival celebrates ethnic music and dance.
words.ex_cn: 这个节日庆祝民族音乐和舞蹈。
words.en: Ethnic relates to a group of people who have a common national or cultural tradition.

words.tr: adj. 人种学的；人种志学的；
words.ex: The anthropologist wrote an ethnographic study of the tribe.
words.ex_cn: 这位人类学家写了一篇关于这个部落的人种学研究。
words.en: Relating to the scientific description of peoples and cultures with their customs, habits, and mutual differences.

words.ex: He studies ethnomusicology to learn about traditional songs.
words.ex_cn: 他研究民族音乐学以了解传统歌曲。
words.en: Ethnomusicology is the study of music from the cultural and social aspects of the people who make it. It is often considered the anthropology or ethnography of music.

words.tr: n. 精神欢快；兴高采烈
words.ex: He felt euphoria after winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得比赛后感到无比兴奋。
words.en: A feeling or state of intense excitement and happiness.

words.tr: adj. （昆虫）完全社会性的；完全群居的
words.ex: Eusocial insects like ants and bees exhibit highly organized social structures.
words.ex_cn: 像蚂蚁和蜜蜂这样的完全社会性昆虫表现出高度组织的社群结构。
words.en: Eusocial refers to the highest level of social organization in a hierarchical classification, characterized by cooperative brood care, overlapping generations within a colony of adults, and a division of labor into reproductive and non-reproductive groups.

words.ex: The city ordered an evacuation because of the fire.
words.ex_cn: 由于火灾，城市下令疏散。
words.en: The process of moving people from a dangerous place to somewhere safe.

words.ex: He tried to evade the police by driving fast.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过高速驾驶来逃避警察。
words.en: If you evade something, you find a way of not doing something that you really ought to do.

words.ex: The shopkeeper will evaluate the old watch.
words.ex_cn: 店主将估价这块旧手表。
words.en: If you evaluate something or someone, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them, for example about how good or bad they are.

words.ex: The sun makes the puddle evaporate quickly.
words.ex_cn: 太阳使水坑很快蒸发。
words.en: If a liquid evaporates, or if something evaporates it, it changes from a liquid state to a gas, because its temperature has increased.

words.ex: The eventual winner was a young student.
words.ex_cn: 最后的赢家是一位年轻学生。
words.en: An eventual event or situation happens at the end of a process or period of time.

words.ex: It is evident that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is evident, it is easy to see, perceive, or understand.

words.tr:
adj. 恶毒的；
n. 邪恶；罪恶；
words.ex: The evil king punished innocent people.
words.ex_cn: 这个恶毒的国王惩罚了无辜的人。
words.en: Evil is a powerful force that some people believe to exist, and which causes wicked and bad things to happen.

words.ex: The bird evolved from a small dinosaur.
words.ex_cn: 这种鸟由一种小型恐龙演变而来。
words.en: If something evolves or you evolve it, it gradually develops over a period of time into something different and usually more advanced.

words.ex: Smoking can exacerbate asthma.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会使哮喘加重。
words.en: If something exacerbates a problem or bad situation, it makes it worse.

words.ex: He exaggerates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸张自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you exaggerate, you indicate that something is, for example, worse or more important than it really is.

words.ex: Workers excavate the old ruins with shovels.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用铲子挖掘古代遗址。
words.en: To excavate means to dig in the ground in order to find things that have been buried there, such as archaeological remains.

words.ex: The excavation revealed ancient pottery.
words.ex_cn: 挖掘发现了古代陶器。
words.en: The process of digging up and removing earth, especially at an archaeological site.

words.ex: The weather is exceedingly cold today.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气极其寒冷。
words.en: To a very great degree; extremely.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；杰出的；罕见的；特别的；
words.ex: She is an exceptional student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 她是一名卓越的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: An exceptional person or thing has some unusual quality or ability that makes them different from others.

words.tr:
n. 摘录；摘要
v. 摘录；引用
words.ex: He read an excerpt from the book.
words.ex_cn: 他读了这本书的一段摘录。
words.en: An excerpt is a short piece of writing or music which is taken from a larger piece.

words.ex: He ate excessive amounts of candy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了过多的糖果。
words.en: If you describe the amount or level of something as excessive, you disapprove of it because it is more or higher than is necessary or reasonable.

words.ex: The rule excludes children under 12.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则排除了12岁以下的孩子。
words.en: To exclude someone or something means to prevent them from entering a place or taking part in an activity.

words.tr: n. 排除器（等于封隔器）
words.ex: The excluder prevents small animals from entering the house.
words.ex_cn: 这个排除器防止小动物进入房子。
words.en: An excluder is a device or person that prevents something or someone from entering or being included.

words.tr: n. 排除；排斥；被排除在外的事物；
words.ex: The exclusion of students from the test was unfair.
words.ex_cn: 将学生排除在考试之外是不公平的。
words.en: The act of preventing someone or something from entering a place or taking part in an activity.

words.ex: He uses this park exclusively for walking.
words.ex_cn: 他只在这个公园散步。
words.en: If you do something exclusively, you do it only in the way mentioned, and not in any other way.

words.ex: The kidneys excrete waste from the body.
words.ex_cn: 肾脏将废物排出体外。
words.en: If someone excretes waste matter from their body, they get rid of it in faeces, urine, or sweat.

words.ex: We went on an excursion to the mountains last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末我们去山区进行了短途旅行。
words.en: An excursion is a short journey or trip, especially one taken as a leisure activity.

words.ex: The computer will execute the program quickly.
words.ex_cn: 计算机将快速执行该程序。
words.en: To execute means to carry out or put into effect a plan, order, or course of action. It can also refer to the act of legally killing someone as a punishment.

words.tr:
n. 决策人；行政官；管理人员；
adj. 行政的；决策的；
words.ex: The executive decided to launch the new product.
words.ex_cn: 这位决策人决定推出新产品。
words.en: An executive is a person who has a senior management position in a business or other organization.

words.tr: adj. 典范的；可做模范的；惩戒性的
words.ex: He is an exemplary student who always finishes his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名模范学生，总是完成作业。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as exemplary, you think they are extremely good and suitable to be copied by other people.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；例证；例示
words.ex: This example exemplifies the rule clearly.
words.ex_cn: 这个例子清楚地说明了这条规则。
words.en: To exemplify means to be a typical example of something or to give an example of something.

words.tr:
v. 豁免；
adj. 被免除的；
words.ex: The school exempted him from the test.
words.ex_cn: 学校免除了他的考试。
words.en: If someone or something is exempt from a particular rule, duty, or obligation, they do not have to follow it or do it.

words.ex: He exerted pressure on his team to win.
words.ex_cn: 他给他的团队施加了压力以赢得比赛。
words.en: To exert means to use power, influence, or effort to make something happen.

words.ex: He exhale slowly after running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步后慢慢呼出气。
words.en: To exhale means to breathe out air from your lungs.

words.tr:
v. 耗尽；用完；使筋疲力尽
n. 排气管；废气
words.ex: The long hike exhausted him.
words.ex_cn: 这次漫长的徒步旅行让他筋疲力尽。
words.en: If something exhausts you, it makes you so tired, either physically or mentally, that you have no energy left.

words.ex: The report gives an exhaustive list of all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告给出了所有规则的详尽列表。
words.en: If you describe a study, search, or list as exhaustive, you mean that it is very thorough and complete.

words.ex: The king was sent into exile after the revolution.
words.ex_cn: 革命后，国王被流放了。
words.en: Exile is the state of being sent away from one's home country or place of residence, often for political or punitive reasons.

words.ex: The exodus of people from the city happened after the flood.
words.ex_cn: 洪水之后，大批人离开了这座城市。
words.en: An exodus is a situation in which many people leave a place at the same time.

words.tr: v. 确定无罪；免除（罪责）
words.ex: The new evidence helped to exonerate him.
words.ex_cn: 新的证据帮助他洗清了罪名。
words.en: If someone is exonerated, they are proved to be not guilty of a crime or responsible for something bad that happened.

words.tr: adj. 外来的；外国来的；奇异的；
words.ex: The market sells exotic fruits from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个市场出售来自其他国家的外来水果。
words.en: Something that is exotic is unusual and interesting because it comes from or is related to a distant country.

words.tr:
v. 移居国外；把…逐出国外
n. 侨民；移居国外者
adj. 移居国外的；被逐出国外的
words.ex: He decided to expatriate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他决定移居加拿大以追求更好的生活。
words.en: An expatriate is someone who lives in a country that is not their own, often for work or political reasons.

words.tr:
n. 权宜之计；应急办法
adj. 权宜的
words.ex: Closing the factory was an expedient to save money.
words.ex_cn: 关闭工厂是为了省钱的权宜之计。
words.en: An expedient action or solution to a problem is one that is convenient or practical, although it may not be morally right.

words.ex: The team went on an expedition to the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍去山上探险了。
words.en: An expedition is an organized journey that is made for a particular purpose such as exploration.

words.ex: The family reduced their monthly expenditure.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭减少了每月的开支。
words.en: Expenditure is the spending of money on something, or the money that is spent on something.

words.tr:
n. 经验；阅历；
v. 经历；体验；
words.ex: He has a lot of experience in teaching English.
words.ex_cn: 他有丰富的英语教学经验。
words.en: Experience is knowledge or skill in a particular job or activity that you have gained because you have done that job or activity for a long time.

words.tr: n. 专门知识；专门技能；
words.ex: His expertise in computers helps the team solve problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在计算机方面的专门知识帮助团队解决问题。
words.en: Expertise is special skill or knowledge that is acquired by training, study, or practice.

words.ex: My passport will expire next month.
words.ex_cn: 我的护照下个月到期。
words.en: If something such as a contract or a visa expires, it comes to an end or is no longer valid.

words.ex: He gave an explicit answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了明确的答案。
words.en: Something that is explicit is expressed or shown clearly and openly, without any attempt to hide anything.

words.ex: The bomb will explode at noon.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹将在中午爆炸。
words.en: If an object explodes, it bursts loudly and with great force, often causing damage or injury.

words.ex: He exploited the situation to get more money.
words.ex_cn: 他利用这个情况赚了更多钱。
words.en: To exploit someone or something means to use them in a way that benefits you, often unfairly or without considering their rights or feelings. It can also refer to the act of making full use of and deriving benefit from a resource.

words.ex: The exploration of space takes many years.
words.ex_cn: 太空探索需要很多年。
words.en: The act of searching for the purpose of discovery of information or resources.

words.ex: They explore the forest to find hidden caves.
words.ex_cn: 他们探索森林以寻找隐藏的洞穴。
words.en: To explore means to travel over or through an unfamiliar area in order to learn about it or to search for something valuable.

words.tr: n. 爆炸；（感情）爆发；激增；
words.ex: The explosion broke all the windows.
words.ex_cn: 爆炸震碎了所有的窗户。
words.en: An explosion is a sudden, violent burst of energy, for example one caused by a bomb.

words.tr:
n. 输出；出口；
v. 输出；出口；
words.ex: This country is a big export of wheat.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家是小麦的大输出国。
words.en: To send goods to another country for sale.

words.ex: He expounded his ideas clearly in the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上清楚地阐述了他的观点。
words.en: To expound means to explain something in detail, especially a theory, idea, or point of view.

words.ex: He faced expulsion for breaking the school rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反校规而被开除。
words.en: Expulsion is the act of forcing someone to leave a place, especially a school or a country, as a punishment or because they are not wanted there.

words.tr: adj. 精美的；细腻的；强烈的
words.ex: She wore an exquisite dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精美的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is exquisite is extremely beautiful or pleasant, especially in a delicate or refined way.

words.ex: They will extend the deadline by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他们将截止日期延长一周。
words.en: To extend something means to make it longer or larger, or to spread it over a larger area.

words.tr: adj. 广大的；广阔的；广泛的；大量的；
words.ex: He has extensive knowledge of history.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有广博的历史知识。
words.en: Something that is extensive covers a wide area or includes a lot of things.

words.ex: The farmer tried to exterminate the rats.
words.ex_cn: 农夫试图消灭老鼠。
words.en: To exterminate means to kill all the members of a group of people or animals, or to destroy something completely.

words.ex: The external wall of the house is painted blue.
words.ex_cn: 房子的外墙被刷成了蓝色。
words.en: External is used to indicate that something is on the outside of a surface or body, or that it exists, happens, or comes from outside.

words.tr: adj. 灭绝的；熄灭的；绝种的；
words.ex: The dodo is an extinct bird.
words.ex_cn: 渡渡鸟是一种灭绝的鸟。
words.en: If a species of animals or plants is extinct, it no longer has any living members, either in the world or in a particular place.

words.ex: The extinction of dinosaurs happened millions of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 恐龙的灭绝发生在数百万年前。
words.en: The state or process of a species, family, or larger group being or becoming extinct.

words.ex: He extinguished the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水把火扑灭了。
words.en: To extinguish a fire or a light means to stop it burning or shining.

words.tr:
v. 提取；
n. 摘录；提取物；
words.ex: They extract oil from plants.
words.ex_cn: 他们从植物中提取油。
words.en: To remove or take out something, especially by effort or force.

words.ex: The extraction of coal harms the environment.
words.ex_cn: 煤炭的开采对环境有害。
words.en: The process of removing or obtaining something from something else.

words.ex: He joins extracurricular activities after school.
words.ex_cn: 他放学后参加课外活动。
words.en: Extracurricular activities are those that fall outside the realm of the normal curriculum of school or university education, performed by students. Extracurricular activities exist at all levels of education, from 4th-6th, junior high/high school, college and university education.

words.ex: The extraneous noise made it hard to concentrate.
words.ex_cn: 那些无关的噪音让人难以集中注意力。
words.en: Something that is extraneous is not relevant or essential to the subject you are dealing with.

words.ex: She has an extraordinary talent for music.
words.ex_cn: 她具有非凡的音乐天赋。
words.en: Something that is extraordinary is very unusual or remarkable.

words.ex: He made an extrapolation from the data to predict the future.
words.ex_cn: 他根据数据做出了外推以预测未来。
words.en: Extrapolation is the act of estimating or concluding something by assuming that existing trends will continue or a current method will remain applicable.

words.tr: adj. 地球外的；地外的；外星球的；
words.ex: The movie shows an extraterrestrial life form.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一种地球外的生命形式。
words.en: An extraterrestrial is a creature that comes from or exists outside the planet Earth.

words.tr:
adj. 极度的；
n. 极端；极端的事物；
words.ex: He felt extreme pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后感到极度疼痛。
words.en: If you describe something as extreme, you mean that it is very great in degree or intensity.

words.tr: n. 织物；（建筑物的）结构；
words.ex: The dress is made of soft fabric.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子是由柔软的织物制成的。
words.en: Fabric refers to cloth or other material produced by weaving together cotton, nylon, wool, silk, or other threads. It can also refer to the basic structure of a building or a system.

words.ex: He has a facial scar from an accident.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上有一道因事故留下的疤痕。
words.en: Facial means relating to the face or designed for use on the face.

words.tr: v. 促进；使便利；使容易；
words.ex: The teacher facilitates learning by asking questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来促进学习。
words.en: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.

words.tr: n. 设施；特色功能；特定场所；资质；
words.ex: The school has a new sports facility.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校有一个新的体育设施。
words.en: A facility is a place, building, or service that is designed for a particular purpose.

words.tr: n. 派系；派系斗争；内讧
words.ex: The faction argued loudly about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 这个派别就新规定激烈争论。
words.en: A faction is a group of people within a larger group who have different opinions and beliefs from the rest of the group.

words.tr:
n. 因素；要素；倍数；
v. 把…因素包括进去；
words.ex: Weather is a factor in the game's outcome.
words.ex_cn: 天气是比赛结果的一个因素。
words.en: A factor is one of the things that affects an event, decision, or situation.

words.ex: The faculty of engineering has many labs.
words.ex_cn: 工程学院有许多实验室。
words.en: A faculty is a group of departments in a university or college that specialize in a particular subject or group of subjects, or the teachers in such a group.

words.ex: He has faith in his ability to win.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己赢得比赛有信心。
words.en: Strong belief in the doctrines of a religion, based on spiritual conviction rather than proof.

words.ex: The dog follows its owner every day.
words.ex_cn: 狗每天跟随它的主人。
words.en: To go or come after (a person or thing proceeding ahead); move or travel behind.

words.ex: He tried to falsify the report.
words.ex_cn: 他试图篡改报告。
words.en: To falsify means to change something in order to deceive people, or to make a false statement.

words.ex: The accident was fatal.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是致命的。
words.en: If an action or event is fatal, it causes someone's death.

words.ex: The car accident caused one fatality.
words.ex_cn: 这场车祸导致一人死亡。
words.en: A fatality is a death caused by an accident or by violence, or is the fact of causing death.

words.tr: n. 过错；故障；缺陷；断层；
words.ex: It was his fault that the car crashed.
words.ex_cn: 汽车撞车是他的过错。
words.en: A fault is a mistake or a weakness in something or someone.

words.ex: It is feasible to finish the project in one week.
words.ex_cn: 一周内完成这个项目是可行的。
words.en: If something is feasible, it can be done, made, or achieved.

words.ex: The fecundity of the rabbits helped them grow quickly.
words.ex_cn: 兔子的高繁殖力帮助它们迅速增长。
words.en: The ability to produce an abundance of offspring or new growth; fertility.

words.tr: adj. 联邦的；联邦制的；联邦政府的；
words.ex: The federal government passed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 联邦政府通过了一项新法律。
words.en: A federal system of government is one in which there is a central government and separate governments for each of the states or regions.

words.ex: He feigns sleep to avoid talking.
words.ex_cn: 他假装睡觉以避免交谈。
words.en: If someone feigns a particular feeling, attitude, or physical condition, they try to make other people think that they have it or are experiencing it, although this is not true.

words.tr:
n. 女权主义者
adj. 女权主义的
words.ex: She is a feminist who believes in equal rights.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位相信平等权利的女权主义者。
words.en: A feminist is a person who believes in and supports the rights and equality of women.

words.tr: adj. 铁的；亚铁的；含铁的
words.ex: The nail is made of ferrous metal.
words.ex_cn: 这枚钉子是铁制的。
words.en: Ferrous means containing or relating to iron, especially in its divalent state.

words.ex: The doctor checked her fertility to help her get pregnant.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了她的生育力，以帮助她怀孕。
words.en: Fertility refers to the ability to produce offspring or to the quality of being fertile, especially in terms of soil or land.

words.tr: adj. 已受精的；使肥沃（fertilize 的过去式与过去分词）；
words.ex: The fertilized egg will grow into a baby.
words.ex_cn: 已受精的卵子会发育成婴儿。
words.en: Something that is fertilized has had a substance added to it to help plants or crops grow, or has had sperm introduced to an egg to start the process of reproduction.

words.ex: He uses fertilizer to help his plants grow.
words.ex_cn: 他用肥料帮助植物生长。
words.en: A substance that is added to soil to improve the growth of plants.

words.tr: adj. 热烈的；强烈的；热情的
words.ex: He is a fervent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: having or showing very strong and sincere feelings about something

words.ex: The fetal heart rate is monitored during pregnancy.
words.ex_cn: 怀孕期间会监测胎儿的心率。
words.en: relating to a fetus, especially in the womb

words.ex: Please fetch me a glass of water.
words.ex_cn: 请给我拿一杯水来。
words.en: If you fetch something or someone, you go to the place where they are and return with them.

words.tr: adj. 封建的；封建制度的
words.ex: The land was owned by feudal lords.
words.ex_cn: 土地由封建领主拥有。
words.en: Relating to, resembling, or characteristic of feudalism.

words.ex: He eats fiber to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃纤维来保持健康。
words.en: A fiber is a thread or a structure or object resembling a thread, especially one that is used to make cloth or rope.

words.ex: The patient has lung fibrosis from long-term smoking.
words.ex_cn: 这位病人因长期吸烟患有肺纤维化。
words.en: Fibrosis is the thickening and scarring of connective tissue, usually as a result of injury.

words.tr: adj. 易变的；无常的；感情不专的
words.ex: He is fickle and changes his mind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他善变，每天都会改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as fickle, you disapprove of them because they keep changing their mind about what they like or want.

words.ex: The fierce lion chased the deer.
words.ex_cn: 那只凶猛的狮子追赶着鹿。
words.en: A fierce animal or person is very aggressive or angry.

words.ex: He bought a small figurine from the market.
words.ex_cn: 他从市场上买了一个小雕像。
words.en: A figurine is a small ornamental statuette.

words.ex: The light bulb has a thin filament.
words.ex_cn: 灯泡有一根细灯丝。
words.en: A filament is a very thin thread or fiber of natural or artificial material.

words.ex: He stored the documents in a metal file.
words.ex_cn: 他把文件存放在一个金属档案盒里。
words.en: A file is a box or folded piece of heavy paper or plastic in which letters or documents are kept. As a verb, to file means to put documents in a file or to officially record something.

words.tr:
v. （因发言冗长）妨碍（会议的进程）
n. （议会中为拖延表决的）冗长演说
words.ex: The senator used a filibuster to delay the vote on the bill.
words.ex_cn: 参议员使用阻挠议事行动来拖延对该法案的投票。
words.en: A filibuster is a tactic used in a legislative assembly to prevent a measure from being brought to a vote. It is most commonly associated with the U.S. Senate, where a senator or a group of senators may extend debate on a proposal indefinitely to delay or entirely prevent a decision on it.

words.tr:
v. 过滤；
n. 过滤器；
words.ex: She filters the water before drinking it.
words.ex_cn: 她在喝水之前过滤水。
words.en: A filter is a device or a method that removes unwanted substances from something such as water, air, or light, by passing it through a special material or system.

words.ex: He was a successful financier who made his fortune in the stock market.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位成功的金融家，在股市中赚取了他的财富。
words.en: A financier is a person who is skilled in managing large amounts of money, especially someone who controls or lends large sums of money to businesses or governments.

words.ex: The book has a finite number of pages.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的页数是有限的。
words.en: Something that is finite has a definite fixed size or extent.

words.ex: The government made a fiscal decision to lower taxes.
words.ex_cn: 政府做出了降低税收的财政决定。
words.en: Fiscal is used to describe something that relates to government money or public money, especially taxes.

words.tr: adv. 五倍地；五重地; adj. 五倍的；五重的
words.ex: The company's profits have increased fivefold over the past decade.
words.ex_cn: 过去十年里，公司的利润增长了五倍。
words.en: Fivefold means five times as much or as many, or consisting of five parts or elements.

words.tr: n. 固定物；固定装置；固定成员
words.ex: The shelf is a fixture in the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 这个架子是厨房里的固定物。
words.en: A fixture is a piece of equipment or furniture which is fixed in position in a building or vehicle.

words.ex: The fjord was surrounded by steep cliffs.
words.ex_cn: 峡湾被陡峭的悬崖包围。
words.en: A fjord is a long, narrow, deep inlet of the sea between high cliffs, typically formed by submergence of a glaciated valley.

words.tr:
n. 公寓；
adj. 平坦的；扁平的；(轮胎)瘪了的；平淡无味的；
adv. 直接地；
words.ex: He lives in a small flat in London.
words.ex_cn: 他住在伦敦的一间小公寓里。
words.en: Something that is flat is level and smooth, with no curved, high, or hollow parts.

words.ex: He used a roller to flatten the dirt.
words.ex_cn: 他用滚筒把泥土压平。
words.en: To flatten something means to make it flat or flatter, or to knock it down to the ground.

words.ex: He likes to flaunt his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢炫耀他的新车。
words.en: If you flaunt something, you show it off in a way that is intended to attract people's attention and make them envious.

words.ex: The cake has a sweet flavor.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕有一种甜味。
words.en: The flavor of a food or drink is its taste, especially a pleasant or distinctive one.

words.tr:
n. 刚长齐羽毛学飞的幼鸟
adj. 新形成的；无经验的
v. 羽毛长成；用羽毛盖上；装上羽毛；“fledge”的现在分词
words.ex: The fledgling bird tried to fly for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 这只幼鸟第一次尝试飞翔。
words.en: A fledgling is a young bird that has just grown its feathers and is learning to fly. It can also refer to a person or organization that is new and inexperienced.

words.ex: She is flexible with her schedule.
words.ex_cn: 她的日程安排很灵活。
words.en: Able to change or be changed easily according to the situation.

words.ex: He flipped the pancake with a spatula.
words.ex_cn: 他用铲子快速翻转了煎饼。
words.en: To flip something means to turn it over quickly one or more times, or to make something do this.

words.tr: adj. 轻率的；轻浮的；不严肃的
words.ex: His flippant remarks annoyed everyone at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他轻率的言论让会议上的每个人都感到恼火。
words.en: If you describe a person or what they say as flippant, you are criticizing them because you think they are not taking something as seriously as they should.

words.tr:
n. （鸟或羊）群；（人）群；
v. 聚集；群集；
words.ex: A flock of birds flew over the field.
words.ex_cn: 一群鸟飞过田野。
words.en: A flock is a group of birds, sheep, or goats, or a large group of people. It can also refer to a soft material for stuffing cushions, quilts, etc., made from wool or cotton. As a verb, it means to gather or move in a flock.

words.tr: v. 繁荣兴旺；茁壮成长；
words.ex: The business flourishes in the new market.
words.ex_cn: 这家企业在新市场中繁荣兴旺。
words.en: If something flourishes, it is successful, active, or common, and developing quickly and strongly.

words.ex: The price of oil fluctuates every day.
words.ex_cn: 油价每天都在波动。
words.en: To fluctuate means to change or vary frequently and unpredictably.

words.ex: The stock market shows daily fluctuation.
words.ex_cn: 股票市场每天都有波动。
words.en: A fluctuation is a change in something, especially in a continuous process such as temperature, prices, or levels of activity.

words.tr:
n. 流体；流质；
adj. 流动的；
words.ex: Water is a common fluid.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种常见的流体。
words.en: A fluid is a substance that can flow and change its shape easily, such as a liquid or a gas.

words.ex: The fluorescent lamp lights up the room quickly.
words.ex_cn: 荧光灯很快照亮了房间。
words.en: Fluorescent substances produce bright light of a particular color when they are exposed to light of a different wavelength.

words.tr:
v. 集中；聚焦；
n. 中心点；焦点；
words.ex: He needs to focus on his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他需要集中精力做作业。
words.en: If you focus on a particular topic or if your attention is focused on it, you concentrate on it and think about it, discuss it, or deal with it, rather than dealing with other topics.

words.ex: The farmer piled up fodder for the cows.
words.ex_cn: 农夫为奶牛堆了一堆饲料。
words.en: Fodder is food that is given to cows, horses, and other animals.

words.tr: n. 民间传说；民俗学；民间风俗；
words.ex: The old man told us a folklore about a dragon living in the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 老人给我们讲了一个关于住在山里的龙的民间传说。
words.en: Folklore is the traditional stories, customs, and habits of a particular community or nation.

words.tr: n. 民风；社会习俗；习惯
words.ex: In that village, folkway tells people how to greet each other.
words.ex_cn: 在那个村庄，风俗习惯告诉人们如何互相打招呼。
words.en: Folkways are the traditional behavior or way of life of a particular community or group of people.

words.ex: The doctor examined the ovarian follicles during the ultrasound.
words.ex_cn: 医生在超声检查中检查了卵巢卵泡。
words.en: A follicle is a small cavity or sac in the body, especially one in the skin that contains the root of a hair.

words.tr:
v. 搜寻；（动物）觅食；
n. 饲料；草料；
words.ex: The bear forages for berries in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这只熊在森林里搜寻浆果。
words.en: If you forage, you search for food or other supplies. Forage can also refer to food for animals, especially when it is grown or collected.

words.tr: n. 搜寻（食物）的人；四处寻找的人；抢劫者；
words.ex: The forager collects berries from the forest.
words.ex_cn: 搜寻食物的人从森林里采摘浆果。
words.en: A forager is someone who searches for food or provisions in the wild.

words.tr: v. 觅食；给……提供食物（forage 的现在分词...；
words.ex: Birds are foraging for worms in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在花园里觅食虫子。
words.en: Foraging is the act of searching for food or provisions.

words.tr:
n. 预测；预报；
v. 预测；预报；
words.ex: The weather forecast says it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 天气预测说明天会下雨。
words.en: If you forecast future events, you say what you think is going to happen in the future.

words.tr: n. 丧失抵押品赎回权
words.ex: The bank initiated foreclosure proceedings after the borrower defaulted on the mortgage.
words.ex_cn: 借款人在抵押贷款违约后，银行启动了丧失抵押品赎回权的程序。
words.en: The legal process by which a lender takes control of a property, evicts the homeowner and sells the home after a homeowner is unable to make full principal and interest payments on his or her mortgage, as stipulated in the mortgage contract.

words.ex: I cannot foresee what will happen tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我无法预知明天会发生什么。
words.en: If you foresee something, you expect and believe that it will happen.

words.ex: The outcome is foreseeable.
words.ex_cn: 结果是可以预见的。
words.en: If a future event is foreseeable, you know that it will happen or that it can happen, because it is a natural or obvious result of something else that you know.

words.ex: The dark clouds foreshadow a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something foreshadows an event or situation, it suggests that it will happen.

words.ex: The dark clouds foreshadow a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
